text: EX-10.2 3 ex10-2.htm EX-10.2 Exhibit 10.2 CONSULTING AGREEMENT This CONSULTING AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) dated as of November 9, 2026 and effective as of [*] 2026 (the “Effective Date”), is made and entered into between NOMAD Power Solutions, Inc. (a Delaware corporation) (the “Company”), and Michael Hilmer, an individual (the “Consultant”). For the avoidance of doubt, the Consultant is engaged solely as a consultant to the Company, and any election of the Consultant to the Board or appointment as Executive Chairman shall occur, if at all, only as provided in Section 1. WHEREAS, the Company desires to engage the Consultant to provide certain consulting services described on Exhibit A (the “Services”) to the Company pursuant to the terms and conditions of this Agreement; WHEREAS, the Consultant has agreed to perform the Services as an independent consultant; WHEREAS, the Board of Directors of the Company (the “Board”) may, at its option and in its sole discretion, elect the Consultant to the Board and appoint the Consultant to serve as the Executive Chairman of the Board of the Company, upon the terms and subject to the conditions hereinafter set forth or as modified by the board with consultant consent; and WHEREAS, the Consultant has the necessary skills and qualifications to serve as the Executive Chairman of the Board and has agreed to serve as such if so elected and appointed, upon the terms and subject to the conditions hereinafter set forth. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the above premises and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which hereby are acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: 1. Independent Consultant. During the term of this Agreement, Consultant will perform the Services in a diligent and professional manner, and in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations. The Company, through the action of its Board, hereby engages the Consultant, and the Consultant will serve the Company, as a consultant. Unless and until the Board, at its option and in its sole discretion, elects the Consultant as a member of the Board and appoints the Consultant as the non-employee Executive Chairman of the Board of directors of the Company (“Executive Chairman”), the Consultant shall serve solely as a consultant to the Company and shall not be, or hold himself out as, a director, officer or Executive Chairman of the Company. The Board is under no obligation to make any such election or appointment. If the Board so elects and appoints the Consultant (the date of such appointment, the “Appointment Date”), the Consultant shall thereafter serve as Executive Chairman during the term of this Agreement, subject to the Company’s governing instruments and applicable law, and shall perform the Services set forth in Exhibit A. 2. Duties, Term, and Compensation. The Consultant’s term of engagement, compensation and provisions for payment thereof are detailed in the attached Exhibit B, and which collectively are hereby incorporated by reference. 3. Expenses. The Company will reimburse the Consultant for all reasonable business expenses Consultant incurs in conducting his duties hereunder, pursuant to the Company’s usual expense reimbursement policies, but in no event later than ninety (90) days after the end of the calendar month following the month in which such expenses were incurred by the Consultant; provided that the Consultant supplies the appropriate substantiation for such expenses no later than the end of the calendar month following the month in which such expenses were incurred by the Consultant. 4. Confidentiality. The Consultant acknowledges that during the engagement it will have access to and become acquainted with various trade secrets, inventions, innovations, processes, information, records and specifications owned or licensed by the Company and/or used by the Company in connection with the operation of its business including, without limitation, the Company’s business and product processes, methods, customer lists, accounts and procedures. The Consultant agrees that it will not disclose any of the aforesaid, directly or indirectly, or use any of them in any manner, either during the term of this Agreement or at any time thereafter, except as required in the course of this engagement with the Company. All files, records, documents, blueprints, specifications, information, letters, notes, media lists, original artwork/creative, notebooks, and similar items relating to the business of the Company, whether prepared by the Consultant or otherwise coming into the Consultant’s possession, shall remain the exclusive property of the Company. The Consultant shall not retain any copies of the foregoing without the Company’s prior written permission. Upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement, or whenever requested by the Company, the Consultant shall immediately deliver to the Company all such files, records, documents, specifications, information, and other items in his possession or under his control. The Consultant confirms that all restrictions in Section 4 are reasonable and valid, and any defenses to the strict enforcement thereof by the Company are waived by the Consultant. The provisions of this Section shall survive any termination of this Agreement. 5.Material Non-Public Information . Consultant acknowledges that, in connection with this Agreement, Consultant may receive information concerning the Company or its securities that constitutes material non-public information (“MNPI”) within the meaning of the U.S. federal securities laws, including the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder. Consultant further acknowledges that it is aware, that the United States securities laws prohibit any person who has MNPI about an issuer from purchasing or selling securities of that issuer, or from communicating that information to any other person under circumstances in which it is reasonably foreseeable that such person is likely to purchase or sell those securities. 6. Conflicts of Interest; Performance of Duties. The Consultant represents that it is free to enter into this Agreement, and that this engagement does not violate the terms of any agreement between the Consultant, any of its personnel or owners and any third party. Further, the Consultant, in rendering the Services, shall not utilize any invention, discovery, development, improvement, innovation, or trade secret in which it does not have a proprietary interest. 7. Other Business Activities: The Consultant agrees that it or any of its personnel or owners are not, and during the Term of this Agreement shall not be, engaged or employed in any business, trade, profession, or other activity that would create a conflict of interest with the Company. If any such actual or potential conflict arises during the Term of this Agreement, the Consultant shall immediately notify the Company in writing. If the Company determines, in its sole discretion, that the conflict is material, the Company may terminate the Agreement immediately upon written notice in accordance with provisions under “Term” under Exhibit B. 8. Indemnification and D&O Insurance: Consultant shall have full responsibility for applicable withholding taxes for all compensation paid to Consultant under this Agreement, and for compliance with all applicable labor and employment requirements with respect to Consultant’s self-employment, franchise tax, worker’s compensation insurance coverage requirements and U.S. immigration visa requirements. Consultant shall indemnify, defend and hold Company harmless from any liability for, or assessment of, any claims or penalties with respect to such withholding taxes, labor or employment requirements including, without limitation, any liability for, or assessment of, withholding taxes imposed on Company by the relevant taxing authorities with respect to any compensation paid to Consultant. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Company shall defend and indemnify the Consultant in his capacity as a consultant to the Company and, from and after the Appointment Date, as a director and Executive Chairman of the Company to the fullest extent permitted under the Delaware General Corporation Law (“DGCL”). The Company shall also maintain a policy for indemnifying its officers and directors, including but not limited to the Consultant, for all actions permitted under the DGCL taken in good faith pursuit of their duties for the Company, including but not limited to maintaining an appropriate level of Directors and Officers Liability coverage and maintaining the inclusion of such provisions in the Company’s by-laws or certificate of incorporation, as applicable and customary. The rights to indemnification shall survive any termination of this Agreement. 9. Independent Contractor. This Agreement shall not render the Consultant an employee, partner, agent of, or joint venturer with the Company for any purpose. The Consultant is and will remain an independent Consultant in his relationship with the Company. The Consultant will receive an IRS Form 1099 from the Company, and the Consultant shall be solely responsible for all federal, state, and local taxes. The Consultant shall have no claim against the Company hereunder or otherwise for vacation pay, sick leave, retirement benefits, social security, worker’s compensation, health or disability benefits, unemployment insurance benefits, or employee benefits of any kind. The Consultant agrees to indemnify and save the Company harmless from and against any and all assessments, losses or penalties actually incurred by the Company in respect of any unpaid taxes or other fees and charges by the Consultant which are charged back to the Company, including, without limitation, contributions to any pension/retirement plans, employment insurance or workers compensation premiums. 10. Successors and Assigns. All of the provisions of this Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective heirs, if any, successors, and assigns. 11. Choice of Law. The laws of the state of New York shall govern the validity of this Agreement, the construction of its terms and the interpretation of the rights and duties of the parties hereto. 12. Arbitration. Any controversies arising out of the terms of this Agreement or its interpretation (“Disputes”) shall be settled in New York in accordance with the rules of the American Arbitration Association, and the judgment upon award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. The parties hereto shall attempt in good faith to settle any Dispute by mutual discussions within thirty (30) days after the date that one party gives notice to the other parties of such a Dispute. If the Dispute is not resolved within such period, the Dispute shall be settled by binding arbitration. This Section 12 shall survive the performance or any earlier termination of this Agreement. 13. Submission to Jurisdiction. Each of the Parties irrevocably submits to the jurisdiction of the courts of the State of New York. 14. Headings. Section headings are not to be considered a part of this Agreement and are not intended to be a full and accurate description of the contents hereof. 15. Waiver. Waiver by one party hereto of breach of any provision of this Agreement by the other shall not operate or be construed as a continuing waiver. 16. Assignment. The Consultant shall not assign any of his rights under this Agreement, or delegate the performance of any of his duties hereunder, except as set forth herein, without the prior written consent of the Company. 17. Notices. All notices required or permitted to be given under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been given and received (a) when personally delivered, or delivered by same-day courier; or (b) on the third business day after mailing by registered or certified mail, postage prepaid, return receipt requested; or (c) upon delivery when sent by prepaid overnight express delivery service (e.g., FedEx, UPS); or (d) when sent by email and upon the receipt by the sending party of written confirmation by the receiving party; provided, however, that an automated email confirmation of delivery or read receipt shall not constitute such confirmation; and, in any case addressed to either party, and in the case of the Company, at its normal business address, and in the case of Consultant, at his residential address or other address provided, which address may be updated by either party in writing from time to time. 18. Modification or Amendment. No amendment, change or modification of this Agreement shall be valid unless in writing signed by the parties hereto. 19. Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed originally or electronically, and any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Signatures provided electronically (including by .pdf, DocuSign, or other electronic signature platform) shall be deemed original signatures. 20. Entire Agreement. This Agreement sets forth the entire understanding of the Parties hereto with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior agreements, promises, statements, representations, negotiations, and understandings, written or oral, with respect to matters covered hereby. 21. Unenforceability of Provisions. If any provision of this Agreement, or any portion thereof, is held to be invalid and unenforceable, then the remainder of this Agreement shall nevertheless remain in full force and effect. [Signature Page Follows] IN WITNESS WHEREOF the undersigned have executed this Agreement as of the day and year first written above. NOMAD Power Solutions, Inc. Consultant By: /s/ Geordan Pursglove By: /s/ Michael Hilmer Name: Geordan Pursglove Name: Michael Hilmer Title: Chief Executive Officer Title: Consultant EXHIBIT A DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES Part I – Consulting Services. Commencing on the Effective Date, Consultant agrees to provide the following Services to the Company: (a) Developing the Company’s budget and go-to-market strategy; (b) Analyzing the Company’s organizational readiness; (c) Commencing discussions with bankers, funding partners and analysts regarding the Company’s vision for 2027; and (d) Assisting with packaging large data center deals and rental strategies, and performing such other duties as the Board may require from time to time. Part II – Executive Chairman Services. From and after the Appointment Date, if any, the Services shall also include the following: (a) Serving as Executive Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company and leading the Board in the performance of its responsibilities; (b) Working with the Board of Directors of the Company to develop and implement the Company’s strategic plan; and (c) Performing such other duties of the Executive Chairman of the Company customarily related to this function in an organization of the size and nature of the Company, and performing such other duties as may be determined and assigned by the Board from time to time and required by the Company’s governing instruments. EXHIBIT B TERM AND TERMINATION: This engagement shall commence on, and shall be effective as of, October 1, 2026, and shall be renewable on a month-to-month basis at the discretion of the Company unless earlier terminated by the Consultant for any reason upon not less than ten (10) business days’ notice given to the Company. The Company may terminate this Agreement upon ten (10) business days’ notice for any reason. In the event of termination prior to the end of a month, the Company shall pay the Consultant on a pro-rata basis any compensation then due and payable for any services completed up to and including the date of such termination. COMPENSATION: The Company will pay the Consultant compensation at the rate of $20,000 per month. This salary will be subject to periodic review and adjustments at the Company’s discretion. TITLE: The Consultant’s title shall be Consultant unless and until the Appointment Date, if any, from and after which the Consultant’s title shall be Executive Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

title: Bunker Hill Silver Corp.
text: EX-10.1 7 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 Bunker Hill Mining Corp. 1099 McKinley Ave. Kellogg, ID 83837 BINDING TERM SHEET CONSULTING AGREEMENT – PRESIDENT & CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER Parties: Bunker Hill Mining Corp. (“ Bunker Hill ” or the “ Company ”), a Nevada corporation, and 101252098 Saskatchewan Ltd. (the “ Consultant ”), which will provide the services of its principal, Galen McNamara (the “ Executive ”). Transaction: Bunker Hill’s acquisition of Silver47 Exploration Corp. (“ Silver47 ”) under the arrangement agreement dated August 20, 2026 (the “ Arrangement Agreement ” and the transaction, the “ Silver47 Transaction ”). “ Closing ” means the effective time of the Silver47 Transaction. Structure: Consulting engagement under which the Consultant provides the Executive’s services to the Company as an independent contractor (the “ Services ”). The Consultant is responsible for all taxes and remittances on its fees and will cause the Executive to comply with the obligations in this term sheet that apply to him. The Services and fees begin at Closing. Long-Form Agreement: The parties will negotiate in good faith and execute a long-form consulting agreement reflecting this term sheet (the “ Long-Form Agreement ”) within 60 days after Closing. If it is not signed within that period, this term sheet remains binding, and the Consultant’s Amended and Restated Executive Consulting Agreement with Silver47 dated December 1, 2025 (the “ Silver47 Agreement ”) applies to the Services, with necessary changes, on all matters this term sheet does not address. Officer Parity: A term marked “Officer Parity” will be consistent with, and no more or less favourable to the Consultant than, the corresponding terms of the agreements of the Company’s other executive officers in effect at Closing (the “ Officer Agreements ”). Role: President & Chief Investment Officer, reporting to the Chief Executive Officer. The mandate covers capital allocation, M&A and corporate development, exploration, investor relations and financial evaluation, as described in the job description attached as Schedule A. The Executive will comply with the Company’s policies applicable to its executive officers, including its insider trading policy. Board: The Executive will be appointed a director at Closing and nominated for election while the Services continue, subject to applicable law and the Board’s fiduciary duties. No separate director fees are payable (Officer Parity). On termination of the Services, the Executive will resign as a director and officer of the Company and its affiliates. Location: Greater Vancouver, with time at the Bunker Hill Mine and travel as the role requires. Outside Activities: The Executive’s role as CEO of Manhattan Uranium and his existing private ventures (as disclosed to the Board before Closing) are permitted, given that the Executive commits to step back to executive director, and then non-executive director, of Manhattan Uranium as soon as practicable. New roles are permitted unless the Board, acting reasonably, determines they are directly competitive. All outside activities must not materially reduce the Services and are subject to the Company’s conflict of interest, confidentiality and insider trading policies. Fee: C$420,000 per year, payable monthly in arrears. Incentives: Short-term incentive target of 70% of the fee and long-term incentive target of 100% of the fee, with plan terms, performance metrics, vesting and payment timing subject to Officer Parity. The 2026 short-term incentive will be pro-rated from Closing. Expenses and Advisory Costs: Reasonable expenses, including travel, reimbursed in accordance with the Company’s policies as applied to its executive officers (Officer Parity). Termination Outside the change of control period described below, the Company will pay or provide: without Just Cause or for Good Reason: (a) a lump sum equal to one times the sum of the fee and the target short-term incentive (the “ Severance Payment ”); (b) a pro-rata target short-term incentive for the year of termination; (c) full vesting of unvested equity awards, subject to the plan terms; and (d) accrued fees and expenses in line with Company’s expense reimbursement policy. The Executive’s service to Silver47 before Closing is credited as service for all purposes of this term sheet and the Long-Form Agreement. Neither the Consultant nor the Executive has any duty to mitigate, and no amount payable under this term sheet is subject to reduction or offset on account of any other engagement, income or amount earned. Good Reason: Any of the following without the Consultant’s consent: (a) a material adverse change in the Executive’s title, duties or reporting; (b) elimination of the position; (c) a reduction in the fee; (d) a required relocation outside Greater Vancouver; or (e) a successor’s failure to assume the Long-Form Agreement in writing. Notice and cure mechanics are subject to Officer Parity. The Silver47 Transaction and this engagement are not Good Reason. Just Cause: As defined in the Silver47 Agreement, with written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure where the conduct is capable of cure. Resignation: 60 days’ written notice with active service provided during the notice period. The Company may waive the active service requirement in the Company’s sole discretion. Change of Control: If the Company terminates the Services without Just Cause, or the Consultant terminates them for Good Reason, within 60 days before or 12 months after a Change of Control (Officer Parity), the Company will pay two times the sum of the fee and the target short-term incentive in place of the Severance Payment, plus the other entitlements above, including full vesting. “ Change of Control ” has the meaning given in the Officer Agreements and excludes the Silver47 Transaction and any internal reorganization (including the Company’s change of name). D&O Protection: Indemnity agreement in the form provided to the Company’s other directors and officers (Officer Parity). D&O insurance covering the Executive while he serves, on terms no less favourable than those for other current and former directors and officers. Silver47 Entitlements: Entitlements accrued under the Silver47 Agreement as of Closing, including the change of control payment disclosed in the Arrangement Agreement disclosure letter, (the “ Silver47 Entitlements ”) are not affected by this term sheet, the Long-Form Agreement or any release. To avoid duplication, neither the Silver47 Transaction nor this engagement will give rise to Good Reason or any termination entitlement under the Silver47 Agreement, and no amount will be paid under both agreements for the same termination or period of service. The Company may enforce this on behalf of Silver47. Restrictive Covenants: At Closing, the Executive will sign, in his personal capacity, a confidentiality, non-solicitation, non-competition and intellectual property agreement with the Company in the form attached as Schedule B. Under it: (a) the non-competition covenant is limited to the Silver Valley, Idaho, for 12 months after termination, and does not apply after a termination without Just Cause, for Good Reason or following a Change of Control; and (b) the confidentiality, intellectual property and 12-month non-solicitation covenants apply whatever the reason for termination. Assignment: The Consultant may not assign this term sheet. The Company may assign it only to a successor that assumes it in writing. Governing Law: British Columbia law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the British Columbia courts, except that equity awards are governed by the applicable plan and the indemnity agreement by Nevada law. Conditions: This term sheet takes effect at Closing, subject to approval by the Board of Bunker Hill and the Executive signing the agreement attached as Schedule B. It terminates automatically if the Arrangement Agreement is terminated before Closing. Disclosure: The Company may disclose the Executive’s appointment and the material terms of this term sheet, and may file it, as required by securities laws (including on Form 8-K) and stock exchange rules. Binding Effect: This term sheet is binding on and enforceable against the parties from Closing, whether or not the Long-Form Agreement is signed. Accepted and agreed to as of the 5th day of November, 2026. BUNKER HILL MINING CORP. By: /s/ Sam Ash Sam Ash Chief Executive Officer 101252098 SASKATCHEWAN LTD. By: /s/ Galen McNamara Galen McNamara Authorized Signatory SCHEDULE “A” JOB DESCRIPTION – PRESIDENT & CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER 1. Services Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, and working closely with the Chief Financial Officer, the General Manager, Idaho Operations, the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, and the Board, the President & Chief Investment Officer will lead the Company’s investment, corporate development and capital allocation functions. The objective of the role is to deploy the Company’s capital into the highest-return opportunities while maintaining a disciplined balance between growth, liquidity, technical risk and shareholder dilution. The President & Chief Investment Officer will also be responsible for the Company’s marketing and investor relations profile, and the Company’s investor relations, exploration and financial evaluation functions will report to the position. The duties described in this Schedule are not exhaustive and may be modified by the Company from time to time, consistent with the position. Position Summary ● Development and maintenance of the Company’s long-term investment strategy, aligned with the Company’s strategic plan, commodity outlook, operating capability and shareholder-return objectives; ● Leadership of the Company’s capital allocation framework, prioritizing investment across organic growth at the Idaho operation, exploration and resource expansion, processing optimization, brownfield development, acquisitions and strategic investments; ● Identification, evaluation, structuring and execution of acquisition, merger, joint venture, royalty, streaming, earn-in and divestiture opportunities; ● Leadership of commercial, strategic, technical, financial and risk-based due diligence on prospective transactions, coordinating external advisers in collaboration with the General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer; ● Evaluation of capital projects at the Idaho operation, working with the General Manager and technical team to translate operating opportunities into bankable investment cases; ● Preparation of investment memoranda, valuation analyses, sensitivity analyses and recommendations for the Chief Executive Officer, executive team, any Investment Committee and the Board; ● Maintenance of robust financial models for the Idaho operation and the Company’s growth initiatives; ● Oversight of the Company’s investor relations function and marketing profile, and support to the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer in communicating the Company’s growth strategy and value-creation plan to the investment community; ● Support of the Company’s engagement with lenders, strategic investors, royalty and streaming counterparties and potential acquisition partners; ● Coordination with the Chief Financial Officer on budgeting, forecasting, financing strategy and the allocation of capital between operations, growth, debt repayment and shareholder returns; ● Support of the Board and its committees in reviewing material investments, acquisitions, divestitures, financing proposals and strategic alternatives; ● Leadership and development of the investor relations, exploration and financial evaluation functions; and ● Such other duties consistent with the position as may be assigned from time to time. Key Responsibilities 1. Investment Strategy & Capital Allocation ● Develop and maintain the Company’s long-term investment strategy and capital allocation framework ● Establish investment criteria, hurdle rates, risk tolerances and post-investment review processes, for approval by the Board or the applicable committee ● Monitor the performance of completed investments against approved business cases and recommend corrective action where required 2. Mergers, Acquisitions & Divestitures ● Lead the identification, screening and evaluation of acquisition, merger, joint venture, royalty, streaming, earn-in and divestiture opportunities ● Develop transaction structures, valuation ranges, negotiation strategies and integration or separation plans ● In coordination with the General Counsel, support the negotiation of confidentiality agreements, letters of intent, exclusivity arrangements and definitive transaction agreements ● Manage transaction execution through signing and closing, and oversee post-closing integration, value capture and performance reporting 3. Organic Growth & Project Investment ● Evaluate capital projects at the Idaho operation, including mine-life extension, resource conversion, exploration programs, mill and processing improvements, infrastructure upgrades and cost-reduction initiatives ● Review and challenge technical assumptions, including mine plan, resource model, metallurgical recovery, capital and operating costs, permitting, schedule and commodity prices ● Support the prioritization of exploration and resource-development spending to maximize value per dollar invested ● Ensure proposed investments are consistent with the Company’s ESG, permitting, community-relations and regulatory obligations 4. Financial Analysis & Valuation ● Lead discounted cash flow, net present value, internal rate of return, payback, break-even and scenario analyses ● Maintain financial models incorporating commodity-price scenarios, exchange rates, tax, royalties, capital expenditure, operating costs and financing assumptions ● Assess the impact of proposed transactions on earnings, cash flow, balance-sheet strength, leverage, liquidity, ownership dilution and market capitalization ● Provide independent, commercially rigorous analysis to challenge management assumptions and support Board decision-making 5. Capital Markets & Investor Relations ● Oversee the Company’s investor relations function and marketing profile in accordance with the Company’s Disclosure Policy ● Support the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer in communicating the Company’s growth strategy, investment pipeline and valuation narrative to institutional investors, analysts, brokers and strategic shareholders ● Prepare investment-related content for investor presentations, conferences, roadshows, annual information forms, management information circulars and securities filings. All such content is subject to review in accordance with the Company’s Disclosure Policy, and scientific and technical information is subject to review and approval by a Qualified Person under NI 43-101 and S-K 1300 ● Monitor peer-company valuations, capital markets conditions, commodity trends, sector transactions and investor sentiment 6. Risk Management & Governance ● Identify and assess commercial, technical, financial, regulatory, political, environmental and reputational risks associated with investment opportunities ● Ensure investment decisions are supported by appropriate due diligence, independent technical review, legal review and Board or committee approval ● Ensure investment processes comply with the Company’s policies, applicable securities laws, and the requirements of each stock exchange or quotation system on which the Company’s securities are listed or quoted 7. Leadership & Team Development ● Lead and develop the investor relations, exploration and financial evaluation functions ● Foster effective coordination across operations, finance, legal and technical teams ● Select and manage external financial, technical and tax advisers in accordance with the Company’s delegation of authority 2. Performance Review The Executive’s performance will be reviewed at the end of each calendar year to assess performance and to inform compensation decisions, including any short-term incentive award. Performance objectives will be established annually by the Chief Executive Officer, subject to Board approval, and may include objectives such as: ● Quality, discipline and strategic fit of investment opportunities presented ● Successful execution of acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures or other strategic transactions ● Value created through capital projects, resource growth, operating improvements or portfolio decisions ● Accuracy and robustness of valuation, modelling and investment recommendations ● Effective coordination with operations, finance, legal, technical and Board stakeholders ● Contribution to investor confidence, capital markets positioning and shareholder value ● Compliance with governance, disclosure, confidentiality and risk-management requirements The objectives listed above are illustrative only, may be changed by the Company from time to time, and do not create any entitlement to a short-term incentive award or other compensation, which remains subject to the term sheet and the discretion of the Board. The Consultant will cause the Executive to perform these duties, and other duties appropriate to the position, using his best efforts; acting honestly and in good faith with a view to the best interests of the Company and its shareholders; and exercising the standard of care, skill and diligence that a reasonably prudent person would exercise in comparable circumstances in the position of President & Chief Investment Officer, or a similar position, of a publicly listed mining company. SCHEDULE “B” CONFIDENTIALITY, NON-SOLICITATION, NON-COMPETITION AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AGREEMENT THIS AGREEMENT is made as of November 5, 2026 between Galen McNamara (the “ Executive ”) and Bunker Hill Mining Corp. (“ Bunker Hill ”). WHEREAS: (A) Bunker Hill and 101252098 Saskatchewan Ltd. (the “ Consultant ”), of which the Executive is the principal, have entered into a binding term sheet dated November 5, 2026 under which the Consultant provides the services of the Executive as President & Chief Investment Officer of Bunker Hill (that term sheet, together with any long-form agreement that replaces it, the “ Consulting Agreement ”); (B) in that role, the Executive will have access to confidential information of Bunker Hill and its affiliates and subsidiaries (collectively, the “ Bunker Hill Group ”); and (C) Bunker Hill would not enter into the Consulting Agreement without the Executive’s agreement to the covenants in this Agreement. NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of Bunker Hill entering into the Consulting Agreement, the equity awards for which the Executive is eligible under it, and other good and valuable consideration (the receipt and sufficiency of which the Executive acknowledges), the parties agree as follows: 1. Definitions. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Agreement, including “Change of Control”, “Good Reason”, “Just Cause”, “Services” and “Termination Date”, have the meanings given in the Consulting Agreement. 2. Confidential Information. (a) “ Confidential Information ” means all information, in any form, relating to the Bunker Hill Group or its business that is not generally available to the public. It includes property information, geological and technical data, studies and models; market information and plans; information about joint venture and strategic partners, shareholders and investors; transaction opportunities; and financial information, strategies, costs and pricing. (b) The Executive will keep Confidential Information confidential and will not disclose or use it, during the Services or at any time after, except (i) as necessary to perform the Services, (ii) with Bunker Hill’s prior written consent, (iii) where the information becomes public other than through a breach by the Executive or the Consultant, or (iv) as required by law, after giving Bunker Hill prompt notice where lawful. 3. Ownership and Intellectual Property. (a) All notes, data, files, models, reports and other materials produced by the Executive in performing the Services, or relating to Confidential Information, belong exclusively to Bunker Hill. The Executive will return all copies to Bunker Hill on request and, in any event, on the Termination Date. (b) All inventions, improvements, discoveries and other work product made or conceived by the Executive, alone or with others, in performing the Services or using Bunker Hill Group resources or Confidential Information (the “ Subject Inventions ”) are the exclusive property of Bunker Hill. The Executive will promptly disclose them, assign all rights in them to Bunker Hill on request, waive any moral rights in them, and give reasonable assistance, during and after the Services, to protect or enforce them. (c) This section does not apply to work product relating to the outside activities permitted under the Consulting Agreement that does not use Confidential Information. 4. Non-Solicitation. During the Services and for 12 months after the Termination Date, whatever the reason for termination, the Executive will not, directly or indirectly: (a) offer employment or engagement to any employee or contractor of the Bunker Hill Group, or to anyone who held that role in the six months before the Termination Date; or (b) solicit or contact any shareholder or business partner, or prospective shareholder or business partner, of the Bunker Hill Group to divert that relationship away from the Bunker Hill Group or for any purpose competitive with or harmful to it. General advertising that is not targeted at Bunker Hill Group personnel is not a breach of paragraph (a). 5. Non-Competition. (a) During the Services and for 12 months after the Termination Date, the Executive will not, directly or indirectly and in any capacity, own, operate, manage, finance or acquire, or bid to do any of those things in respect of, any business with mining operations or projects in the Silver Valley of Shoshone County, Idaho, including the Coeur d’Alene Mining District. (b) This section does not apply if the Services are terminated by Bunker Hill without Just Cause, by the Consultant for Good Reason, or for any reason after a Change of Control. (c) This section does not restrict (i) a passive holding of up to [2]% of any class of a publicly traded issuer’s securities, or (ii) the outside activities permitted under the Consulting Agreement. 6. Enforcement. (a) The Executive agrees that the covenants in this Agreement are reasonable and necessary to protect the Bunker Hill Group’s confidential information and goodwill. (b) A breach or threatened breach of this Agreement would cause Bunker Hill irreparable harm. In addition to any other remedy, Bunker Hill is entitled to seek interim and permanent injunctive relief. (c) Each covenant in this Agreement is separate and distinct. If any covenant is found to be unenforceable, the others are not affected. 7. Survival. This Agreement survives the termination of the Services and of the Consulting Agreement for the periods stated in it. 8. Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Province of British Columbia and the federal laws of Canada that apply there. The parties attorn to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of British Columbia. 9. Independent Legal Advice. The Executive acknowledges that he has had the opportunity to obtain independent legal advice before signing this Agreement. 10. Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts and delivered electronically. Each counterpart is an original, and together they form one agreement. IN WITNESS WHEREOF the parties have signed this Agreement as of the date first written above. GALEN McNAMARA /s/ Galen McNamara Signature BUNKER HILL MINING CORP. By: /s/ Sam Ash Sam Ash Chief Executive Officer

text: EX-10.1 4 tm2629086d1_ex10-1.htm EXHIBIT 10.1 Exhibit 10.1 TERMINATION AND RELEASE AGREEMENT This Termination and Release Agreement (this “ Agreement ”), dated as of November 10, 2026, is entered into by and among Braemar Hotels & Resorts Inc., a Maryland corporation (“ Braemar ”) and its Affiliates party hereto (collectively, the “ Braemar Parties ”), on the one hand, and Ashford Inc., a Nevada corporation (“ Ashford ”) and its Affiliates party hereto (collectively, the “ Ashford Parties ”), on the other hand. The Braemar Parties and the Ashford Parties are sometimes referred to herein individually as a “ Party ” or collectively as the “ Parties .” WHEREAS , (i) Braemar, Braemar Hospitality Limited Partnership, Braemar TRS Corporation (collectively, the “ Company ”), and (ii) Ashford Inc., and Ashford Hospitality Advisors LLC (collectively, the “ Advisor ”) are parties to that certain Fifth Amended and Restated Advisory Agreement, dated as of April 23, 2018, as amended by that certain Enhanced Return Funding Program Agreement and Amendment No. 1 to the Fifth Amended and Restated Advisory Agreement, dated as of January 15, 2019, as further amended by that certain Amendment No. 2 to the Fifth Amended and Restated Advisory Agreement, dated as of August 16, 2021, and as further amended by that certain Amendment No. 3 to the Fifth Amended and Restated Advisory Agreement, dated as of May 21, 2026 (as so amended, the “ Advisory Agreement ”), and that certain Letter Agreement, dated as of August 26, 2025, as amended by that certain Amendment to Letter Agreement, dated as of December 22, 2025 (the “ Letter Agreement Amendment ” and the letter agreement as so amended, the “ Letter Agreement ”), pursuant to which, among other things, the Advisory Agreement will terminate upon the consummation of a Company Sale Transaction (as defined in the Letter Agreement) and payment of the Company Sale Fee, Accrued Fees and Master Agreement Termination Fee (collectively, the “ Termination Payments ”) to the Ashford Parties; WHEREAS , in the Letter Agreement, Advisor agreed to accept the Company Sale Fee in lieu of (and as payment in full of) the Full Termination Payment (as defined in the Letter Agreement), which represented a material discount to the Full Termination Payment; WHEREAS , the special committee of the board of directors of Braemar, composed entirely of independent directors, was formed to evaluate a range of strategic alternatives available to Braemar and, following such evaluation, determined that it is in the best interests of Braemar and its stockholders to pursue the termination of the Advisory Agreement and the internalization of management of Braemar (the “ Internalization ”) in order to maximize shareholder value, and the board of directors of Braemar subsequently approved the consummation of a Company Sale Transaction, the payment of the Termination Payments and the Internalization; WHEREAS , a Company Sale Transaction was consummated on July 14, 2026 upon the sale of the Ritz-Carlton Sarasota (Sarasota, Florida), the Hotel Yountville (Yountville, California) and the Bardessono Hotel and Spa (Yountville, California) and in connection therewith, the Company has paid the Termination Payments to Ashford in full simultaneously with the execution of this Agreement immediately following which the Advisory Agreement and the Letter Agreement shall be terminated (other than such provisions of such agreements identified expressly as surviving in Annex I hereto) (the “ Advisory Agreement Termination ”); WHEREAS , as a result of the Advisory Agreement Termination, (i) Braemar is required to reimburse Ashford for all expenses due and payable to Ashford pursuant to Section 5 of the Advisory Agreement and (ii) Ashford is required to pay over all money collected and held for the account of Braemar, subject to certain permitted deductions, pursuant to Section 12.5(d) of the Advisory Agreement (the amounts described in the foregoing clauses (i) and (ii), the “ Settlement Amounts ”), and the agreed upon estimate of the Settlement Amounts is set forth on the settlement statement attached hereto as Annex II (the “ Settlement Statement ”); WHEREAS , in connection with the Company Sale Transaction, the Company has paid Ashford the net amount of the Settlement Amounts (the “ Expense Reimbursement ”) simultaneously with the execution of this Agreement; WHEREAS , the Company and the Advisor desire to waive the sixty (60) day notice period required by Section 1 of the Letter Agreement Amendment (the “ Advisory Agreement Notice Period ”) in connection with the Advisory Agreement Termination and, as a result thereof, the Advisor is forfeiting any fees that would otherwise have accrued and be payable to the Advisor during such notice period had it not been so waived (the “ Notice Waiver and Fee Forfeiture ”); and WHEREAS , in furtherance of the Internalization, immediately following the payment of the Termination Payments and the Expense Reimbursement, the Parties desire to terminate the Advisory Agreement, the Letter Agreement and each of the other Contracts set forth on Annex I (other than such provisions of such agreements identified expressly as surviving in Annex I hereto) (collectively, the “ Terminating Contracts ”). For good and valuable consideration, including the termination of the Terminating Contracts and the Notice Waiver and Fee Forfeiture, the Parties hereto hereby agree as follows: Section 1. Definitions. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings given to them in the Advisory Agreement or, if not defined therein, in the Letter Agreement. The terms defined in this Section 1 , whenever used herein, shall have the following meanings for all purposes of this Agreement: “ Affiliate ” of a Person shall mean (i) any other Person that is directly or indirectly (through one or more intermediaries) controlled by, under common control with, or controlling such Person, or (ii) any other Person in which such Person has a direct or indirect equity interest constituting at least a majority interest of the total equity of such other Person. For purposes of this definition, “control” shall mean the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of any Person or the power to veto major policy decisions of any Person, whether through the ownership of voting securities, by contract or otherwise. For the avoidance of doubt, for purposes of this Agreement, Braemar and its controlled Affiliates shall not be considered Affiliates of the Ashford Parties. “ Braemar Master Project Management Agreement ” means the Braemar Master Project Management Agreement, dated as of August 8, 2018, by and among Braemar TRS Corporation, CHH III Tenant Parent Corp., RC Hotels (Virgin Islands), Inc., Braemar Hospitality Limited Partnership and Project Management LLC (“ Premier ”), as amended by that certain Amendment No. 1 to the Braemar Master Project Management Agreement, as further amended by that certain Amendment No. 2 to the Braemar Master Project Management Agreement, dated as of February 12, 2024, by and among Braemar TRS Corporation, CHH III Tenant Parent Corp., RC Hotels (Virgin Islands), Inc., Premier Project Management LLC, and Braemar Hospitality Limited Partnership. “ Contract ” shall mean any written or oral agreement, contract, side letter, subcontract, lease, sublease, license, sublicense, instrument, note, bond, mortgage, indenture, arrangement, understanding, guarantees, indemnities, commitment or other binding obligation, in each case, entered into between or among any Braemar Party or any of their Affiliates, on the one hand, and any Ashford Party or any of their Affiliates, on the other hand. “ Effective Time ” means such time as immediately follows the receipt of the Termination Payments and the Expense Reimbursement by Ashford. 2 Section 2. Termination. (a) Other than as specifically set forth herein, at the Effective Time, (i) each of the Braemar Parties, on behalf of itself and each of its Affiliates, and each of the Ashford Parties, on behalf of itself and each of its Affiliates, hereby settle, terminate, and cancel, as applicable, in all respects without any further liability to, or obligations of, the Braemar Parties and the Ashford Parties that are party thereto, the Terminating Contracts and all rights and obligations of any kind or nature of the parties to the Terminating Contracts pursuant thereto (other than such provisions of such agreements identified expressly as surviving in Annex I hereto), and (ii) each Party, on behalf of itself and each of its Affiliates, hereby irrevocably waives any and all notice periods, cure periods, waiting periods or other similar procedural requirements that may be required under any Terminating Contract as a condition to the termination, cancellation or non-renewal thereof (which, for the avoidance of doubt, includes the Advisory Agreement Notice Period). For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2 shall terminate, cancel or otherwise affect the surviving provisions of the Terminating Contracts expressly set forth in Annex I hereto, which shall remain in full force and effect in accordance with their respective terms. (b) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, the Parties acknowledge and agree that (i) the Braemar Master Project Management Agreement is continuing in effect solely as an accommodation to Braemar, at Braemar’s request, in order to complete, in the most efficient and cost-effective manner, capital expenditure projects that were commenced prior to the date hereof and (ii) Braemar has the right, in its sole discretion, to terminate the Braemar Master Project Management Agreement upon (A) five (5) days’ prior written notice to Ashford and (B) payment to Ashford of all outstanding amounts that are accrued but unpaid for services rendered under the applicable agreement as of the date of such termination. (c) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, to effect an orderly transition of information technology systems and to maintain, during such transition, the Braemar Parties’ internal control over financial reporting required under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 in connection with the Braemar Parties’ reporting obligations under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 in good faith and in the normal course of business, and to support related internal and external audit requirements, the Ashford Parties shall permit: (i) Employees of the Braemar Parties who, as of the date hereof, use the Ashford Parties’ Oracle enterprise resource planning system (“ Oracle ”), to continue to access such systems solely with respect to data relating to the operation of Braemar’s business (“ Braemar Data ”) on a read-only basis for a period beginning from the date hereof and ending upon the filing of the Braemar Form 10-K for the year ending December 31, 2026, which shall be filed no later than March 31, 2027. For the avoidance of doubt, such continued access to Oracle shall not be deemed to reinstate, extend or create any Contract, and nothing in this Section 2(c) shall obligate the Ashford Parties to maintain any particular system beyond the ordinary course of their own business and under no circumstances may employees of the Braemar Parties have write or edit access to Oracle or access to any data other than Braemar Data. The Ashford Parties reserve the right to remove such access from employees of the Braemar Parties with ten (10) days’ written notice; provided, that Ashford may so remove access from such employees immediately and without notice if Ashford believes in good faith that any Braemar Party or their employees or representatives have violated this clause (i). (ii) The Braemar Parties to complete the IT data migration of designated Microsoft Outlook email account files, OneDrive account files and Sharepoint files (in accordance with the scope and procedures agreed by the Ashford Parties and Braemar Parties) promptly and in no event to exceed thirty (30) days after the date hereof. 3 Section 3. Transition. (a) Books and Records. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Advisory Agreement, as promptly as reasonably practicable following the Effective Time, the Advisor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to, in accordance with Section 10 of the Advisory Agreement and in accordance with the scope and procedures mutually agreed by the Ashford Parties and the Braemar Parties, deliver to Braemar all books, records, documents, files and contracts of the Braemar Parties in the possession or control of any Ashford Party, including the Braemar Parties’ general ledger and sub-ledgers and their fixed asset, tax, payroll, contract, insurance, litigation, and Board and committee records, in the electronic formats in which they are maintained in the ordinary course. (b) Insurance. (i) The Ashford Parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to continue to administer, in the ordinary course and consistent with past practice, each insurance policy issued prior to the Effective Time under which one or more of the Braemar Parties (or any of their current or former directors, officers or employees) and one or more of the Ashford Parties are insureds, including the directors’ and officers’ liability tail policy taking effect in connection with the transactions contemplated in this Agreement (collectively, the “ Shared Policies ”). The Ashford Parties shall have primary responsibility for all Shared Policies and will use commercially reasonable efforts to continue to administer and pursue coverage, or cause to be administered or for coverage to be so pursued, in the ordinary course, all losses or claims (whenever occurring) under such policies, including those that are for the benefit of the Braemar Parties and any natural person insureds who may cease serving in an insured capacity. For the avoidance of doubt, the Ashford Parties shall have primary responsibility for all claims for coverage under the Shared Policies, including without limitation those arising out of occurrences, facts, circumstances, events or matters prior to or after the Effective Time. (ii) The Ashford Parties and Braemar Parties shall keep each other reasonably informed of, and shall promptly provide to each other copies of all material notices concerning any claim under a Shared Policy related to any Braemar Party or any of its current or former directors, officers or employees. (iii) The Parties agree that no insurance claim submitted under any Shared Policy shall be settled without the mutual consent of both Parties and Ashford Hospitality Trust, Inc., which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. (iv) None of the Parties, nor Ashford Hospitality Trust, Inc. shall knowingly take any action after the Effective Time that would reasonably be expected to cause any Shared Policy to be terminated, amended, or materially altered in terms of the scope of coverage. (c) Further Cooperation. (i) In addition to the foregoing, each Ashford Party shall, at the reasonable request of Braemar, cooperate with and provide reasonable assistance to the Braemar Parties, consistent with Section 12.5(d)(iv) of the Advisory Agreement, in connection with (A) effecting an orderly transition of the management of the Braemar Parties’ business and assets to the Braemar Parties, (B) any litigation, arbitration, investigation or other proceeding brought by or involving a third party (whether pending, threatened or hereafter commenced) arising out of or relating to the business or operations of the Braemar Parties prior to the Effective Time, including by making available relevant books, records, and documents and making current employees and representatives of the Ashford Parties reasonably available for interviews, depositions or testimony, and (C) any other matters arising out of or relating to the Terminating Contracts or the operation of the Braemar Parties’ business prior to the Effective Time, in each case, excluding any Claims released pursuant to Section 4 or any matter as to which cooperation is addressed elsewhere in this Agreement. 4 (ii) In addition to the foregoing, each Braemar Party shall, at the reasonable request of any Ashford Party, cooperate with and provide reasonable assistance to the Ashford Parties in connection with (A) effecting an orderly transition of the management of the Braemar Parties’ business and assets to the Braemar Parties, (B) any litigation, arbitration, investigation or other proceeding brought by or involving a third party (whether pending, threatened or hereafter commenced) arising out of or relating to the business or operations of the Braemar Parties prior to the Effective Time, including by making available relevant books, records and documents and making current employees and representatives of the Braemar Parties reasonably available for interviews, depositions or testimony, and (C) any other matters arising out of or relating to the Terminating Contracts or the operation of the Braemar Parties’ business prior to the Effective Time, in each case, excluding any Claims released pursuant to Section 4 or any matter as to which cooperation is addressed elsewhere in this Agreement. (iii) Each Party shall bear its own costs and expenses incurred in connection with cooperation provided under clause (i) or clause (ii) above, except that, if such cooperation relates to an Ashford Indemnifiable Claim or a Braemar Indemnifiable Claim, the costs and expenses thereof shall be governed by Section 5 . Section 4. Releases. (a) Effective immediately following the receipt of the Termination Payments and the Expense Reimbursement by Ashford, each of the Braemar Parties, on behalf of itself and each of its Affiliates, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases and discharges the Ashford Parties and their Affiliates, and each of their respective past, present or future partners, equityholders, Affiliates, directors, managers, officers, employees, counsel, agents and successors and assigns (the “ Ashford Released Parties ”) from any and all Claims, which it has now or may have in the future, whether known or unknown, based upon any events that have occurred prior to the Effective Time, and agrees that it shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to assert any Claim against any Ashford Released Party; provided , however , that nothing in this Section 4 shall constitute a release or discharge of (i) any Claims arising under or relating to this Agreement, (ii) the surviving provisions of the Terminating Contracts expressly set forth in Annex I hereto, or (iii) any Claims arising under or relating to any Contracts between the Braemar Parties, on the one hand, and the Ashford Parties, on the other, that are not Terminating Contracts. (b) Effective immediately following the receipt of the Termination Payments and the Expense Reimbursement by Ashford, each of the Ashford Parties, on behalf of itself and each of its Affiliates, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases and discharges its past or present directors and officers and the Braemar Parties and their Affiliates, and each of their respective past, present or future partners, equityholders, Affiliates, directors, managers, officers, employees, counsel, agents and successors and assigns (the “ Braemar Released Parties ”) from any and all Claims, which it has now or may have in the future, whether known or unknown, based upon any events that have occurred prior to the Effective Time, and agrees that it shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to assert any Claim against any Braemar Released Party; provided , however , that nothing in this Section 4 shall constitute a release or discharge of (i) any Claims arising under or relating to this Agreement, (ii) the surviving provisions of the Terminating Contracts expressly set forth in Annex I hereto, or (iii) any Claims arising under or relating to any Contracts between the Braemar Parties, on the one hand, and the Ashford Parties, on the other, that are not Terminating Contracts. (c) Each of the Ashford Released Parties and the Braemar Released Parties not a party hereto shall be an intended third-party beneficiary of this release and its related terms and shall have the right to enforce the provisions of this Section 4 and its related terms as if such Person were a party hereto. 5 Section 5. Indemnification and Advancement. (a) The Braemar Parties, on behalf of themselves and each of their Affiliates, shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Ashford Released Parties from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, claims, demands, actions, judgments, costs, expenses (including attorneys’ fees), arising out of or relating to any breach by any of the Braemar Parties of any covenant or obligation under this Agreement, whether or not involving a claim by a third party (hereinafter an “ Ashford Indemnifiable Claim ”). The Braemar Parties shall advance all expenses reasonably estimated by any third-party advisor to be incurred, or that are actually incurred, by any of the Ashford Released Parties (hereinafter “ Ashford Indemnitee ”) in connection with an Ashford Indemnifiable Claim within five (5) business days after receipt of a statement requesting such advances from time to time, whether prior to or after final disposition of any Ashford Indemnifiable Claim. Such advances shall be unsecured and interest free and shall be made without regard to Ashford Indemnitee’s ability to repay the expenses and without regard to Ashford Indemnitee’s ultimate entitlement to indemnification. Ashford Indemnitee shall be entitled to continue to receive advancement of expenses unless and until the matter of Ashford Indemnitee’s entitlement to indemnification hereunder has been finally adjudicated by court order or judgment from which no further right of appeal exists. Ashford Indemnitee hereby undertakes to repay such amounts advanced only if, and to the extent that, it ultimately is determined that Ashford Indemnitee is not entitled to be indemnified. Ashford Indemnitee shall qualify for advances upon the execution and delivery of this Agreement, which shall constitute the requisite undertaking with respect to repayment of advances made hereunder and no other form of undertaking shall be required to qualify for advances made hereunder. (b) The Ashford Parties, on behalf of themselves and each of their Affiliates, shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Braemar Released Parties from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, claims, demands, actions, judgments, costs, expenses (including attorneys’ fees), arising out of or relating to any breach by any of the Ashford Parties of any covenant or obligation under this Agreement, whether or not involving a claim by a third party (hereinafter a “ Braemar Indemnifiable Claim ”). The Ashford Parties shall advance all expenses reasonably estimated by any third-party advisor to be incurred, or that are actually incurred, by any of the Braemar Released Parties (hereinafter “ Braemar Indemnitee ”) in connection with a Braemar Indemnifiable Claim within five (5) business days after receipt of a statement requesting such advances from time to time, whether prior to or after final disposition of any Braemar Indemnifiable Claim. Such advances shall be unsecured and interest free and shall be made without regard to Braemar Indemnitee’s ability to repay the expenses and without regard to Braemar Indemnitee’s ultimate entitlement to indemnification. Braemar Indemnitee shall be entitled to continue to receive advancement of expenses unless and until the matter of Braemar Indemnitee’s entitlement to indemnification hereunder has been finally adjudicated by court order or judgment from which no further right of appeal exists. Braemar Indemnitee hereby undertakes to repay such amounts advanced only if, and to the extent that, it ultimately is determined that Braemar Indemnitee is not entitled to be indemnified. Braemar Indemnitee shall qualify for advances upon the execution and delivery of this Agreement, which shall constitute the requisite undertaking with respect to repayment of advances made hereunder and no other form of undertaking shall be required to qualify for advances made hereunder. Section 6. Company Sale Fee. (a) The Parties acknowledge and agree that, as provided in Section 2(a) of the Letter Agreement, the Company Sale Fee is a negotiated amount that the Advisor agreed to accept in lieu of (and as payment in full of) the Full Termination Payment, and that Section 5 of the Letter Agreement survives the termination of the Letter Agreement as provided in Annex I and shall continue to bind the Parties and their respective successors and assigns. (b) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Advisory Agreement, the Letter Agreement or this Agreement, in the event that the Company commences or intervenes to pursue directly an action or proceeding against any Ashford Party challenging (i) the validity or enforceability of this Agreement, the Advisory Agreement or the Letter Agreement or any provision thereof (including, but not limited to, by seeking rescission thereof), or (ii) the amount or payment of the Termination Payments or (iii) seeks recoupment of all or any portion of the Termination Payments, then the amount due and payable to the Advisor by the Company pursuant to Section 12.5(b) of the Advisory Agreement (excluding Accrued Fees) and the Letter Agreement upon a Company Sale Transaction shall be deemed to be the amount of the Full Termination Payment and the Advisor shall be entitled to recover against the Company the amount by which the Full Termination Payment exceeds the Company Sale Fee. This Section 6(b) shall not apply to (A) any action or proceeding commenced by any stockholder of Braemar (whether directly or derivatively), so long as the Company does not intervene to pursue such action or proceeding directly against any Ashford Party; or (B) any proceeding under Section 9(c) of this Agreement. 6 Section 7. Confidentiality. Each Party agrees that, from and after the date hereof, it shall, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, managers, officers, employees, counsel, agents and representatives (collectively, “ Representatives ”) to, keep confidential and not disclose to any third party, and not use for any purpose other than as contemplated by this Agreement, any and all confidential or proprietary information furnished by or on behalf of any other Party or its Affiliates in connection with the Terminating Contracts, the Advisory Agreement, the Letter Agreement, or this Agreement (collectively, “ Confidential Information ”); provided, that Confidential Information shall not include information that (a) is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of a breach of this Section 7 , (b) was already in the possession of the receiving Party or its Representatives on a non-confidential basis prior to disclosure by the disclosing Party, (c) is or becomes available to the receiving Party or its Representatives on a non-confidential basis from a source other than the disclosing Party or its Representatives, provided that such source is not known by the receiving Party to be bound by a confidentiality obligation to the disclosing Party with respect thereto, or (d) is independently developed by the receiving Party or its Representatives without reference to or use of any Confidential Information. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Party or its Representatives may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, legal process or governmental or regulatory authority, provided that such Party shall, to the extent legally permitted, (i) promptly notify the disclosing Party of such requirement prior to any such disclosure and (ii) cooperate with the disclosing Party, at the disclosing Party’s sole cost and expense, in seeking a protective order or other appropriate remedy to limit such disclosure. Each Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Section 7 by any of its Representatives. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Section 7 , (i) the books and records of the Braemar Parties, including those compiled by the Advisor and delivered pursuant to Section 3(a) , are property of the Braemar Parties and shall not constitute Confidential Information of any Ashford Party; (ii) nothing in this Section 7 shall restrict any Party from using or disclosing information as required by law (A) in any filing with, or report to, the Securities and Exchange Commission or any securities exchange, (B) to its auditors, lenders, insurers, counsel and other advisors, or (C) in connection with the defense or prosecution of any litigation, arbitration, investigation or other proceeding; and (iii) as between the Company and the Advisor, Section 11 of the Advisory Agreement shall continue to apply in accordance with Annex I . Section 8. Further Assurances. Each Party, upon the reasonable request from time to time of any other Party, and without further consideration, will use commercially reasonable efforts to, and will cause its respective Affiliates to, do each and every act and thing as may be reasonably necessary to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby and to execute and deliver such additional documents, instruments or other agreements to give effect to the transactions contemplated hereby. Without limiting the foregoing, the Ashford Parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to execute and deliver such UCC termination statements, account signatory changes, notices to lenders, hotel managers, insurers and vendors, and other instruments as Braemar may reasonably request to evidence the termination of the Terminating Contracts and the matters set forth in Section 3 . 7 Section 9. Misallocated Assets or Payments. (a) If, following the date hereof, any right, property, asset or payment that is part of the business or operations of any of the Braemar Parties is found to be held, or is received, by any of the Ashford Parties, the Ashford Parties shall transfer such right, property or asset, or remit such payment, as applicable, to Braemar or its designee promptly (but in the case of a payment obligation, within five (5) business days after any Ashford Party obtains actual knowledge of the receipt of the applicable sum by any Ashford Party). Until such time as the Ashford Parties transfer or remit the foregoing in accordance with this Section 9 , such party shall hold such right, property, asset or payment in trust until such time as the transfer is completed for no additional consideration. (b) If, following the date hereof, any right, property, asset or payment that is part of the business or operations of any of the Ashford Parties is found to be held, or is received, by any of the Braemar Parties, the Braemar Parties shall transfer such right, property or asset, or remit such payment, as applicable, to Ashford or its designee promptly (but in the case of a payment obligation, within five (5) business days of the receipt of the applicable sum by any Braemar Party). Until such time as the Braemar Parties transfer or remit the foregoing in accordance with this Section 9 , such party shall hold such right, property, asset or payment in trust until such time as the transfer is completed for no additional consideration. (c) The Parties acknowledge that the Settlement Amounts are based on good faith estimates of the Parties and therefore the Parties will negotiate in good faith to attempt to agree to any necessary adjustments to such amounts that may be required to reconcile such estimates to actual amounts received or paid after the Effective Time (the net amount of any such adjusted amounts, the “ Final Expense Reimbursement ”) within sixty (60) days following the date hereof (the “ Reimbursement Deadline ”). Such reconciliation will be reasonably documented in a manner acceptable to the Parties in good faith for purposes of their books and records. If the Parties have not agreed upon the Final Expense Reimbursement by the Reimbursement Deadline, the Ashford Parties and the Braemar Parties will each prepare a proposed statement setting forth their respective determination of the Final Expense Reimbursement, together with supporting detail, and such statements shall be submitted within thirty (30) days following the Reimbursement Deadline to BDO USA, LLP or another independent firm of certified accountants mutually selected by the Parties (the “ Accounting Arbitrator ”), who shall determine the Final Expense Reimbursement. The Accounting Arbitrator shall determine the Final Expense Reimbursement within ninety (90) days following the Reimbursement Deadline on the basis of the Advisory Agreement, this Agreement and the statements of the Parties. Absent manifest error, actual and intentional fraud, or willful misconduct, the decision of the Accounting Arbitrator shall be final and binding on the Parties. Upon a determination of the Final Expense Reimbursement, either by agreement of the Parties or by the Accounting Arbitrator, the difference between the Expense Reimbursement and the Final Expense Reimbursement shall be paid by wire transfer of immediately available funds by the applicable Party to the other Party within three (3) business days following such determination. The costs, fees and expenses of the Accounting Arbitrator shall be borne by each Party in the same proportion as the aggregate amount of the disputed amounts submitted to the Accounting Arbitrator with respect to the Final Expense Reimbursement that are unsuccessfully disputed by each such Party (as finally determined by the Accounting Arbitrator) bears to the total amount of disputed amounts so submitted. For the avoidance of doubt, the submission of any matter to the Accounting Arbitrator in accordance with this Section 9(c) shall not constitute a breach of, or a challenge to, this Agreement, the Advisory Agreement or the Letter Agreement. Section 10. Miscellaneous. (a) Governing Law . This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to the conflict of laws principles thereof. 8 (b) WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL . EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ALL RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION, PROCEEDING OR COUNTERCLAIM ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT. (c) Effect; Assignment . This Agreement shall inure to the benefit of and be binding upon the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns. No Party may assign this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the other Parties. (d) Amendment and Modification . This Agreement shall not be altered or otherwise amended in any respect, except pursuant to an instrument in writing signed by the Parties. The waiver by a Party of a breach of any provision of this Agreement shall not operate or be construed as a waiver of any subsequent breach. (e) Counterparts . This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed to be an original, and all of which shall constitute one and the same agreement. (f) Severability . If any provision of this Agreement is held to be prohibited by law or invalid, then such provision shall be ineffective only to the extent of such prohibition or invalidity, without invalidating or affecting in any manner whatsoever the remainder of such provision or the remaining provisions of this Agreement.
