text: EX-10.3 6 tm2629086d1_ex10-3.htm EXHIBIT 10.3 Exhibit 10.3 RELEASE AND WAIVER THIS RELEASE AND WAIVER (this “ Termination Release ”) is made and entered into by and among Richard J. Stockton (the “ Executive ”), Ashford Hospitality Advisors, LLC (the “ Company ”) and Ashford Inc. (“ AINC ”). WHEREAS, the Company, AINC and the Executive entered into that certain Employment Agreement, dated November 14, 2016 (the “ Original Agreement ”), providing certain compensation and severance amounts upon the Executive’s termination of employment; WHEREAS, the Company, AINC and the Executive entered into that certain Amended and Restated Employment Agreement, dated April 1, 2019 (the “ 2019 Agreement ”); WHEREAS, the Company, AINC, Braemar Hotels & Resorts Inc. (“ Braemar ”), Ashford Hospitality Trust, Inc., the Executive and Jordan Jennings entered into that certain Agreement Concerning Personal Relationship, dated February 15, 2022 (the “ Personal Relationship Agreement ”); WHEREAS, the Company and the Executive entered into that certain First Amendment to Amended and Restated Employment Agreement, dated April 1, 2022 (the “ 2022 Agreement ,” and together with the Original Agreement and the 2019 Agreement, the “ Agreement ”); WHEREAS, the Executive has agreed, pursuant to the terms of the Agreement, to execute a release and waiver in the form set forth in this Termination Release in consideration of the Company’s agreement to provide the compensation and severance amounts upon the Executive’s termination of employment set out in the Agreement, and the termination by the Company and AINC of certain restrictive covenants contained in the Agreement; WHEREAS, the Company, AINC and the Executive desire to settle all rights, duties and obligations among them, including without limitation all such rights, duties, and obligations arising under the Agreement or otherwise out of the Executive’s employment by the Company; and WHEREAS, all capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings given them in the Agreement. NOW THEREFORE, intending to be legally bound and for good and valid consideration the sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows: 1. QUALIFYING TERMINATION PAYMENTS AND CONDITIONS. The Executive and the Company acknowledge and agree that the Date of Termination (as defined in the Agreement) is or will be November 10, 2026. Payment of the compensation and severance amounts contained in the Agreement is subject to Executive’s execution and non-revocation of this Termination Release and is due pursuant to the terms described in the Agreement. Consistent with the revocation period described below, no such payment will be due sooner than eight (8) days following the date that Executive executes the Termination Release. 1 2. GENERAL RELEASE BY EXECUTIVE. (a) Except as set forth in Section 2(b) below, the Executive knowingly and voluntarily releases, acquits, covenants not to sue and forever discharges the Company, AINC and all the other Ashford-Related Entities, and its and their respective owners, parents, stockholders, predecessors, successors, assigns, agents, directors, officers, employees, representatives, divisions and subsidiaries (collectively, the “ Releasees ”) from any and all charges, complaints, claims, liabilities, obligations, promises, agreements, damages, causes of action, suits, rights, costs, losses, debts and expenses of any nature whatsoever, known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, foreseen or unforeseen, matured or unmatured (collectively, the “ Claims ”), against them which the Executive or any of his heirs, executors, administrators, successors and assigns ever had, now has or at any time hereafter may have, own or hold by reason of any matter, fact, or cause whatsoever from the beginning of time up to and including the date of this Termination Release, including without limitation all claims arising under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, the Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993, the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, Texas Labor Code Section 21.001, et seq. (Texas Employment Discrimination); Texas Labor Code Section 61.001, et seq. (Texas Pay Day Act); Texas Labor Code Section 62.002, et seq. (Texas Minimum Wage Act); Texas Labor Code Section 201.001, et seq. (Texas Unemployment Compensation Act); Texas Labor Code Section 401.001, et seq., specifically Section 451.001 formerly codified as Article 8307c of the Revised Civil Statutes (Texas Workers’ Compensation Act and Discrimination Issues); and Texas Genetic Information and Testing Law, each as amended, or any other federal, state or local laws, rules, regulations, judicial decisions or public policies now or hereafter recognized. Expressly excluded from this Termination Release are Claims which cannot be waived by law, including any right to receive an award or “bounty” for information provided to any governmental agency (such as the Securities and Exchange Commission) in connection with protected whistleblowing activity. (b) The Executive represents that he has not filed or permitted to be filed against any of the Releasees, any complaints, charges or lawsuits with any court or governmental agency, arbitrator or self-regulatory body and covenants and agrees that he will not seek or be entitled to any personal recovery directly from any of the Releasees in any court or before any governmental agency, arbitrator or self-regulatory body arising out of any matters set forth in Section 2(a) hereof. The foregoing does not prevent the Executive from accepting an award or “bounty” from any governmental agency in connection with protected whistleblowing activity. Nothing herein shall prevent the Executive from seeking to enforce his rights under this Termination Release or the Agreement, including without limitation, the Executive’s right to receive his Accrued Obligations, Severance Payment, Pro-Rated Bonus and Other Benefits as set forth in Section 7(a) and Section 7(b) of the Agreement, and his rights under Section 12 of the Agreement. The parties have agreed that the Severance Payment is $5,524,000, which will be paid to the Executive within 30 days after the Date of Termination, and the Pro-Rated Bonus is $982,000, which will be paid to the Executive at the same time 2026 incentive bonuses are paid to the Company’s other senior executives. The Executive does not hereby waive or release (i) his rights to any benefits under the Company’s employee benefit plans to which he is or will be entitled pursuant to the terms of such plans in the ordinary course; (ii) any rights to indemnification, advancement of expenses or coverage under any directors’ and officers’ liability insurance policy that the Executive has under the Agreement (including Sections 5(e) and 14 thereof), any indemnification agreement, the governing documents of any of the Releasees, or applicable law with respect to his service as an officer, director or employee of the Company or any of the Ashford-Related Entities; or (iii) any rights under any employment, compensation, indemnification or other agreement or arrangement between the Executive and Braemar or any of its subsidiaries entered into on or after the Date of Termination. 2 3. ADEA RELEASE BY EXECUTIVE. The Executive hereby completely and forever releases and irrevocably discharges the Releasees, from any and all Claims arising under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (“ ADEA ”) on or before the date the Executive signs this Termination Release (the “ ADEA Release ”), and hereby acknowledges and agrees that: (i) this Termination Release, including the ADEA Release, was negotiated at arm’s length; (ii) this Termination Release, including the ADEA Release, is worded in a manner that the Executive fully understands; (iii) the Executive specifically waives any rights or claims under the ADEA; (iv) the Executive knowingly and voluntarily agrees to all of the terms set forth in this Termination Release, including the ADEA Release; (v) the Executive acknowledges and understands that any claims under the ADEA that may arise after the date of this Termination Release are not waived; and (vi) the rights and claims waived in this Termination Release, including the ADEA Release, are in exchange for consideration over and above anything to which the Executive was already entitled. 4. GENERAL RELEASE BY COMPANY. The Company and AINC, on behalf of themselves and their affiliates, each do hereby fully, finally and completely release Executive from any and all Claims of any kind or nature arising out of the Executive’s employment with the Company arising from, relating to, or in any way connected with any facts or events occurring on or before the date of this Termination Release; provided, however , that the Executive is not released or discharged from his continuing obligations contained in this Termination Release or the Agreement. 5. NON-DISPARAGEMENT. The Executive covenants and agrees he will not make statements or representations, or otherwise communicate, directly or indirectly, in writing, orally, or otherwise, or take any action which may, directly or indirectly, disparage the Company or its affiliates or their respective officers, directors, employees, advisors, businesses or reputations. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein or in the Agreement shall preclude the Executive from making truthful statements or disclosures that are required by applicable law, regulation or legal process. The Company covenants and agrees that its directors, officers and other employees will not make statements or representations, or otherwise communicate, directly or indirectly, in writing, orally, or otherwise, or take any action which may, directly or indirectly, disparage the Executive or his family or his business or reputation; provided, however , the Company shall have no liability for any communication by its employees (other than its officers) that violates this non-disparagement clause, unless an officer of the Company is made aware of such communication and fails to take appropriate action to enforce this non-disparagement clause on behalf of the Company. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein or in the Agreement shall preclude the Executive or the Company or any of its affiliates or its or their officers and directors from (i) contacting, reporting to, communicating with, responding truthfully to an inquiry from, providing truthful information to, filing a charge or complaint with, cooperating with, making truthful statements under oath in connection with, or otherwise testifying or participating in any investigation, hearing, or other proceeding conducted by or before any federal or state law enforcement, governmental, or regulatory agency or body (such as the U.S. Department of Justice, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the U.S. Department of Labor, or another federal or state law enforcement, governmental, regulatory, or fair employment practices agency) regarding possible or alleged violations of law or unlawful acts in the workplace, or pursuant to applicable whistleblower statutes, and doing so in each instance without prior notice to or authorization from another party or (ii) making truthful statements or disclosures that are required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process. 3 6. REAFFIRMATION OF CONTINUING OBLIGATIONS AS MODIFIED; TERMINATION OF CERTAIN AGREEMENT. The Company agrees that (i) the Executive’s continued service to or employment by Braemar in any capacity after the Date of Termination shall not be a violation of his obligations under Section 10(a) of the Agreement or any other similar agreement between the Company or an affiliate and the Executive that restricts the Executive’s service or employment after the Termination Date; (ii) his obligations under Section 10(b)(i) of the Agreement (as amended in Section 2 of the 2022 Agreement) shall not extend to employees or individual service providers of Braemar (or those persons who were employed or engaged by Braemar within the six months preceding the Date of Termination); and (iii) his obligations under Section 10(b)(ii) of the Agreement (as amended in Section 2 of the 2022 Agreement) shall not extend to Braemar’s business relationships with its current investors, financiers, or other capital providers. Except as modified in the preceding sentence, nothing in this Termination Release shall be deemed to affect or relieve the Executive from any continuing obligation contained in any other agreement with the Company or the Company’s rights with respect thereto. The Executive specifically acknowledges and reaffirms his continuing obligations to the Company under the Agreement (including, for the avoidance of doubt, the modifications to such restrictive covenants, terms and conditions set forth in Sections 2 and 3 of the 2022 Agreement) not modified in the first sentence of this paragraph. The Executive further acknowledges that this reaffirmation is material to this Termination Release, and the Executive acknowledges and agrees that his continuing non-competition and non-solicitation obligations under the Agreement as so modified are reasonable and enforceable and that he will not challenge or violate these covenants. The parties acknowledge and agree that the terms, conditions and restrictions of the Personal Relationship Agreement are terminated as of the Date of Termination. 7. MODIFICATION; WAIVER. No modification or addition hereto or waiver or cancellation of any provision hereof shall be valid except by a writing signed by the party to be charged therewith. No delay on the part of any party to this Termination Release in exercising any right or privilege provided hereunder or by law shall impair, prejudice or constitute a waiver of such right or privilege. 8. SEVERABILITY. If any provision contained in this Termination Release is determined to be void, illegal or unenforceable, in whole or in part, then the other provisions contained herein shall remain in full force and effect as if the provision which was determined to be void, illegal or unenforceable had not been contained herein. 9. COSTS. The parties hereto agree that each party shall pay its respective costs, including attorney’s fees, if any, associated with this Termination Release. 4 10. FULLY UNDERSTOOD; PAYMENTS RECEIVED. By signing this Termination Release, the Executive acknowledges and affirms that he has read and understands the foregoing Termination Release, agrees to the terms of this Termination Release, and acknowledges receipt of a copy of this Termination Release. The Executive also hereby acknowledges and affirms the sufficiency of the compensation and severance amounts recited herein. The Executive further acknowledges that upon receipt of the compensation and severance amounts recited herein, he shall not be entitled to any further payment, compensation or remuneration of any kind from the Company, with respect to the Executive’s employment with the Company or otherwise. 11. NO VIOLATIONS. As a material inducement for the Company to enter into this Termination Release, the Executive represents that: (i) he has not committed any act which is in violation of any federal or state law or regulation or the Company’s or any of the other Ashford-Related Entities’ personnel or conduct and ethics policies or which constitutes a breach of fiduciary duty; (ii) he has no knowledge that any of the Ashford-Related Entities (or their officers, directors or employees) have committed, any act which is in violation of any federal or state law or regulation or the Company’s or any of the other Ashford-Related Entities’ personnel or conduct and ethics policies, which constitutes a breach of fiduciary duty, or have acted in a manner which requires corrective action of any kind that has not already been taken; and (iii) he has not informed any of the Ashford-Related Entities of, and he is unaware of, any violations of any federal or state law or regulation or the Company’s or any of the other Ashford-Related Entities’ personnel or conduct and ethics policies or breach of fiduciary duty. 12. [Intentionally Deleted]. 13. ENTIRE AGREEMENT. This Termination Release contains the entire agreement between the Executive, on one hand, and the Company and AINC, on the other hand, and supersedes any and all prior understandings or agreements with respect to the subject matter hereof, whether written or oral, except as set forth herein. ACKNOWLEDGMENT. The Company hereby advises the Executive to consult with an attorney of his choosing prior to signing this Termination Release and the Executive hereby represents to the Company that he has been offered an opportunity to consult with an attorney prior to signing this Termination Release. The Company also hereby advises the Executive that Executive has up to twenty-one (21) days to consider and sign the Termination Release and up to seven (7) days after signing in which to revoke acceptance by giving notice to Ashford Hospitality Advisors, LLC, Attn: Jim Plohg – General Counsel, 14185 Dallas Parkway, Suite 1200, Dallas, TX 75254, by personal delivery or by mail postmarked no later than the seventh (7 th ) day after the Executive signs the Termination Release. If Executive does not so timely revoke his acceptance, this Termination Release shall become effective and enforceable. The Executive acknowledges and agrees that any changes in the terms of this Termination Release, whether material or immaterial, after the date upon which the Executive first received this Termination Release shall not affect or restart the above-referenced twenty-one (21)-day consideration period. [SIGNATURE PAGE FOLLOWS] 5 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, and intending to be legally bound hereby, the parties hereto have executed this Termination Release as of the day and year first above written. ASHFORD HOSPITALITY ADVISORS, LLC By: /s/ Jim Plohg Name: Jim Plohg Title: Executive Vice President Dated: November 10, 2026 ASHFORD INC. By: /s/ Jim Plohg Name: Jim Plohg Title: Executive Vice President Dated: November 10, 2026 EXECUTIVE: /s/ Richard J. Stockton RICHARD J. STOCKTON Dated: November 10, 2026 6

title: Braemar Hotels & Resorts Inc.
text: EX-10.5 8 tm2629086d1_ex10-5.htm EXHIBIT 10.5 Exhibit 10.5 SEPARATION AGREEMENT (Age 40 and over) This Separation Agreement (this “ Agreement ”) is entered into by Ashford Hospitality Advisors LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the “ Company ”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Ashford Inc., a Nevada corporation (“ AINC ” and, together with the Company and all of AINC’s other subsidiaries and affiliates, the “ Ashford Entities ”), and Justin Coe (the “ Employee ”). The Company and Employee are sometimes referred to collectively in this Agreement as the “ Parties ” and individually as a “ Party .” Recitals WHEREAS , Employee’s employment with the Company will permanently end on November 10, 2026 (the “ Separation Date ”); and WHEREAS , to assist Employee’s transition to other employment, the Parties mutually desire to enter into this Agreement to set forth the Company’s offer and Employee’s acceptance of certain benefits in exchange for and conditioned on Employee’s timely execution and return of this Agreement, and Employee’s post-separation obligations set forth below; and WHEREAS , this Agreement is not being entered into in connection with or in settlement of any claims of alleged discrimination, retaliation, or harassment. NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the mutual promises and undertakings set out below, the sufficiency of which is acknowledged by their signatures below, and intending to be legally bound, the Parties agree as follows: Agreement 1. Separation from Employment and Related Matters . (a) Separation from Employment . Employee’s employment with the Company and status as a service provider to any of the other Ashford Entities and any entities advised by any of the Ashford Entities and any such advised entities’ affiliates, including without limitation Ashford Hospitality Trust, Inc. (“ AHT ”) and Braemar Hotels & Resorts Inc. (“ BHR ”) (together with the Ashford Entities, the “ Ashford-Related Entities ”), will permanently end on November 10, 2026 (the “ Separation Date ”). (b) Final Pay; Effect on Benefit Plans . Employee will receive his/her base salary through the Separation Date at the time required by applicable law. Nothing in this Agreement affects Employee’s accrued and vested benefits under applicable employee benefit plans, or Employee’s right to continue or convert coverage under certain employee benefit plans, including the Company’s group health plan pursuant to the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985 (known as COBRA), at his/her cost and in accordance with the terms of those plans and applicable law. (c) No Further Obligations . By his/her signature below, Employee acknowledges and agrees that upon receiving his/her final paycheck, he/she will have received all the compensation, benefits and paid or unpaid leave to which he/she is entitled, and that, except as provided in Section 2 below, he/she will not be entitled to and will not receive any additional compensation (including any bonus), benefits, paid or unpaid leave from any of the Ashford-Related Entities. SEPARATION AGREEMENT – Page 1 2. Separation Benefit . In consideration of the General Release in Section 3 and the other promises and undertakings of Employee set out in this Agreement, and contingent on Employee’s full performance of those promises and undertakings, the Company will pay (or cause to be paid) to Employee the following separation benefit (the “ Separation Benefit ”): (i) $1,500.00 and (ii) an amount in cash equal to all unpaid deferred cash awards granted to Employee by AHT and BHR that have not vested as of the Separation Date, if any (the “ Unvested Awards ”). The Separation Benefit, less legally required withholdings and deductions, will be paid to Employee by direct deposit or check mailed to Employee’s last address on file with the Company in one lump sum on the Company’s first payroll date that is at least five (5) business days after the Effective Date, but in any event no earlier than November 15, 2026 (defined in Section 10 below). Employee acknowledges and agrees that, upon payment of the Separation Benefit, any and all rights Employee has in the Unvested Awards shall terminate. 3. General Release and Covenant Not to Sue by Employee . (a) In consideration of the Separation Benefit and the other promises and undertakings of the Company set out in this Agreement, and subject to Section 4 below, Employee (for him/herself and anyone claiming through him/her) voluntarily, completely, and unconditionally releases, waives, and forever discharges to the maximum extent permitted by law the Released Parties (defined below) from any and all claims, demands, liabilities, obligations, and causes of action of whatever kind or character, whether vicarious, derivative, or direct, and whether known or unknown (collectively, the “ Claims ”), that he/she now may have or ever has had in any capacity, individually, or as a member of a class, collective, or representative action, against any of the Released Parties, including any right to initiate or participate in any class or collective action with respect to any Claims that are released by this Agreement, and to the maximum extent permitted by law, covenants not to sue or to file or cause to be filed any legal action in any court with the respect to the Claims. (b) The Claims released and waived by this Agreement include without limitation any and all Claims (including for attorneys’ fees): (i) growing out of, resulting from, or connected in any way with Employee’s employment, the ending of his/her employment, or the employment practices of any of the Released Parties; (ii) based on any policy of any of the Ashford-Related Entities, written agreement between Employee and any of the Released Parties, or promise or representation concerning any aspect of the employment relationship or ending of that relationship; (iii) based on any bonus, equity, or other incentive plan or program of any of the Ashford-Related Entities; (iv) based on the common law, such as Claims based on contract or in tort (including for fraudulent inducement), or on any federal, state, or local statutory or constitutional provision that applies or is asserted to apply, directly or indirectly, to his/her employment, the ending of employment, or the employment practices of any of the Released Parties; (v) Claims under any labor or employment practices, employment discrimination, or fair employment practices statute (including without limitation under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 42 U.S.C. § 1981, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (the “ ADEA ”), the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act, the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, the Genetic Information Non-Discrimination Act, the Equal Pay Act, the Fair Labor Standards Act (to the extent permissible by law), the Fair Credit Reporting Act, and the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act, and state-law counterparts); (vi) for severance pay or benefits not expressly provided for in Section 2 above or additional compensation, paid or unpaid leave of any kind, or payment for accrued but unused paid leave; and (vii) based on any other act, conduct, or omission of any of the Released Parties. SEPARATION AGREEMENT – Page 2 (c) The “ Released Parties ” are: (i) the Company; (ii) AINC; (iii) all the other Ashford-Related Entities; (iv) any parent, subsidiary, or affiliate of the entities named or described in clauses (i)-(iii); (v) any predecessor, successor, or assign of the entities named or described clauses (i)-(iv); and (vi) any current or former, officer, director, partner, shareholder, owner, member, manager, joint venturer, trustee, fiduciary, agent, employee, associate, representative, administrator, employee benefit plan sponsored or maintained by, insurer, or attorney of or for the entities and persons named or described in clauses (i)-(v), in any capacity. 4. Exceptions to the General Release and Covenant Not to Sue by Employee; Permitted Activities . (a) Nothing in this Agreement (including the General Release and Covenant Not to Sue by Employee in Section 3 above and the Confidential Information; Return of Property in Section 6) or any other agreement between Employee and any of the Ashford-Related Entities is intended to or does: (i) waive or release any Claims under the ADEA that may arise after the date Employee signs this Agreement; (ii) waive or release Employee’s right to receive the Separation Benefit or to enforce the terms of this Agreement; (iii) waive or release any right of the Employee to challenge the enforceability of this Agreement if permitted by law; (iv) waive or release any administrative Claims for unemployment compensation or workers’ compensation benefits; (v) waive or release any Claims or rights that cannot by law be released, such as any right to receive an award or “bounty” for information provided to any governmental agency in connection with any protected whistleblowing activity; (vi) prevent Employee from contacting, reporting to, communicating with, responding truthfully to an inquiry from, providing truthful information to, filing a charge or complaint with, cooperating with, making truthful statements under oath in connection with, or otherwise testifying or participating in any investigation, hearing, or other proceeding conducted by or before any federal or state law enforcement, governmental, or regulatory agency or body (such as the U.S. Department of Justice, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the U.S. Department of Labor, the National Labor Relations Board, the Occupational Safety and Health Commission, the Texas Workforce Commission-Civil Rights Division, another federal or state law enforcement, governmental, regulatory, or fair employment practices agency) regarding possible or alleged violations of law or unlawful acts in the workplace, including discrimination retaliation, or harassment, or pursuant to applicable whistleblower statutes, and doing so in each instance without prior notice to or authorization from the Company or any of the other Ashford-Related Entities; (vii) assisting another in taking any of the actions in clause (vi); (viii) engaging in any other legally protected or concerted activities, including discussing terms, conditions, or benefits of employment with others for the mutual aid or protection of employees; or (ix) making truthful statements or disclosures that are required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process. SEPARATION AGREEMENT – Page 3 (b) Employee acknowledges and agrees, however, that by signing this Agreement, he/she is forever waiving any right to recover, and will not request or accept, anything of value directly from any of the Released Parties as compensation, damages, or other individual legal relief growing out of, resulting from, or connected in any way with the Claims being released in the General Release in Section 3 above, other than the Separation Benefit, whether sought directly by him/her or by any administrative agency or other public authority, individual, or group of individuals on his/her behalf. The foregoing does not prevent Employee from accepting an award or “bounty” from any governmental agency in connection with protected whistleblowing activity. 5. Limited Release of Employee and Covenant Not to Sue . (a) In consideration of the General Release and Covenant Not to Sue by Employee in Section 3 above and his/her other promises and undertakings set out in this Agreement, the Company (on behalf of itself and AINC) voluntarily, completely, and unconditionally releases, waives, and forever discharges Employee from any and all Claims that it now may have or ever has had against Employee (including for attorneys’ fees) growing out of, resulting from, or in any way associated with Employee’s employment, or the ending of his/her employment, with the Company excepting, however, any claims for fraud, embezzlement, theft, or other illegal acts , and covenants and agrees not to sue or to file or cause to be filed any legal action in any court with respect to the Claims so released. (b) Exceptions to Limited Release of Employee and Covenant Not to Sue; Permitted Activities . Nothing in this Agreement is intended to or does: (i) waive or release the Released Parties’ right to enforce this Agreement or any other agreement between the Parties; (ii) prevent the Released Parties from contacting, reporting to, communicating with, responding truthfully to an inquiry from, providing truthful information to, cooperating with, making truthful statements under oath, or otherwise testifying or participating in any investigation, hearing, or other proceeding being conducted by or before any federal or state law enforcement, governmental, or regulatory agency or body; or (iii) prevent the Released Parties from making truthful statements or disclosures that are required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process. 6. Confidential Information; Return of Property . (a) Acknowledgements Regarding Confidential Information . Employee acknowledges and agrees that: (i) the Ashford-Related Entities are engaged in a highly competitive business; (ii) the Ashford-Related Entities have expended considerable time and resources to develop goodwill with their employees, customers, vendors, and others, and to create, protect, and exploit their Confidential Information (defined below); (iii) the Ashford-Related Entities must continue to prevent the dilution of their goodwill and unauthorized use or disclosure of their Confidential Information to avoid irreparable harm to their legitimate business interests; and (iv) by virtue of his/her position, Employee had access to Confidential Information, the disclosure or unauthorized use of which would irreparably harm the Ashford-Related Entities’ competitive position in the marketplace and dilute their goodwill. SEPARATION AGREEMENT – Page 4 (b) Agreements and Representations Regarding Confidential Information . Accordingly, subject to Section 4(a) above, Employee agrees: (i) that all Confidential Information and Property (defined below) shall remain the sole and exclusive property of the Ashford-Related Entities; (ii) to protect and safeguard all Confidential Information; (iii) to hold all Confidential Information in strictest confidence and to not, directly or indirectly, use any such Confidential Information for his/her own or a third-party’s advantage, benefit, or gain; (iv) unless he/she is authorized to do so by an officer, director, or legal counsel for the Company or AINC, not to disclose or divulge any such Confidential Information to any person other than an officer, director, or employee of, or legal counsel for, the Company or AINC; (v) if Employee believes he/she is compelled by law or legal process to disclose or divulge any Confidential Information, to notify the General Counsel of AINC sufficiently in advance of any such disclosure to allow the Ashford-Related Entities the opportunity to defend, limit, or otherwise protect their interests against such disclosure; (vi) not to recreate or attempt to recreate the Confidential Information; and (vii) not to ask, direct, or authorize another to take any action that would be prohibited by this subsection if undertaken by Employee. Employee represents that he/she has not removed, copied, destroyed, defaced, damaged, or deleted any Confidential Information other than in the proper performance of his/her duties as an employee; he/she has not exported any Confidential Information to, or copied, placed, or saved any Confidential Information on, any computer or electronic storage system (such as a USB thumb drive or other external storage device) other than in the proper performance of his/her duties as an employee; and he/she has not forwarded any Confidential Information to a personal email address. The foregoing does not apply to any Confidential Information of BHR used by Employee solely in connection with, and in furtherance of, Employee’s employment with BHR or any of its affiliates. (c) Return of Property . Employee represents that he/she has returned (or has made arrangements with the Company to return) to Company Human Resources all property belonging to any Ashford-Related Entity, except for items approved in writing by the Company, in good and working condition, including without limitation: (i) physical property such as computers, monitors, printers and related equipment and identification or access card(s) or badge(s); (ii) access codes or passwords to or necessary to access any Company-provided computer, external hard drive or storage device, any Company documents, and any Ashford-Related Entity’s information or security systems; (iii) physical or electronic documents (and all copies thereof) that contain or include information about any Ashford-Related Entity’s business and operations (including without limitation the Confidential Information as defined below); and (iv) any other physical or electronic documents (and all copies thereof) that he/she received from or sent to any employee of any Ashford-Related Entity, or that he/she otherwise had access to during his/her employment (other than copies of personnel, benefit, or payroll documents concerning only him/her) (collectively, the “ Property ”). Employee agrees that if he/she later discovers some Property that he/she has not returned, he/she will contact Company Human Resources as soon as possible to make arrangements to return it. SEPARATION AGREEMENT – Page 5 (d) “ Confidential Information ” for purposes of this Agreement means: (i) all material nonpublic information about any of the Ashford-Related Entities or any of the other Released Parties; (ii) any “trade secret,” as defined by federal and applicable state law, of any of the Ashford-Related Entities or any of the other Released Parties; and (iii) all other confidential or proprietary information or trade secrets of or relating to any of the Ashford-Related Entities or any of the other Released Parties and their current, past, future, or prospective owners, investors, business partners, customers, vendors, capital providers, investments, financings, and suppliers, or otherwise provided to any of the Ashford-Related Entities under an obligation or expectation of confidential treatment. “ Confidential Information ” includes without limitation all documents or information (in whatever form or medium, and all copies thereof whether or not the original was deleted or destroyed) conceived, originated, discovered, or developed in whole or in part by Employee, otherwise disclosed to or obtained by Employee, or to which Employee had access and that concerns or evidences operations; processes; products; business practices; finances; strategies; modes of doing business; performance; development, acquisition, or divestment plans; any proposed business transactions; officers, directors, or shareholders; current or potential investors, capital providers, business partners, customers, vendors, and suppliers; marketing methods; costs; prices; contractual relationships; legal or regulatory status; and Personnel Information. “ Personnel Information ” for purposes of this Agreement means confidential or personal, personally identifiable information about any current or former employees of any Ashford-Related Entity (such as medical, performance, or disciplinary history, financial, or banking records or information, and non-public contact information); Social Security numbers; compilations of personnel data (such as compensation, payroll, or benefits information, or that otherwise contains personally identifiable information); and performance and capabilities of employees, except as such information pertains solely to Employee. Notwithstanding the foregoing, “Confidential Information” does not mean any information of BHR used by Employee solely in connection with, and in furtherance of, Employee’s employment with BHR or any of its affiliates. 7. Other Representations, Promises, and Undertakings of Employee . (a) Assistance and Cooperation . Employee agrees to provide such assistance as may be reasonably requested by the Company relating to matters in which he/she was involved or had responsibility while employed at the sole cost and expense of the Company or other applicable Ashford Entity. Employee further agrees to cooperate with any of the Ashford Entities, at their request, in all contemplated, pending, and future litigation, regulatory actions, investigations, arbitrations, and/or other fact-finding or adjudicative proceedings, public or private, involving matters for which Employee had some responsibility while employed or about which he otherwise had personal knowledge. This obligation includes meeting with the applicable Ashford Entities or their representatives or attorneys at reasonable times at their request, and providing sworn testimony and statements that are truthful, accurate, and complete. The Company or the other applicable Ashford Entity will reimburse Employee upon submission of substantiating documentation for actual and reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by him/her in fulfilling his/her obligations under this subsection (such as travel or parking expense). (b) No Violations . As a material inducement for the Company to enter into this Agreement, Employee represents that: (i) he/she has not committed any act which is in violation of any federal or state law or regulation or the Company’s or any of the other Ashford-Related Entities’ personnel or conduct and ethics policies or which constitutes a breach of fiduciary duty; (ii) he/she has no current, actual knowledge (without any duty to investigate) that any of the Ashford-Related Entities (or their officers, directors or employees) have committed any act which is in violation of any federal or state law or regulation or the Company’s or any of the other Ashford-Related Entities’ personnel or conduct and ethics policies, which constitutes a breach of fiduciary duty, or have acted in a manner which requires corrective action of any kind that has not already been taken; and (iii) he/she has not informed any of the Ashford-Related Entities of, and he/she has no current, actual knowledge (without any duty to investigate) of, any violations of any federal or state law or regulation or the Company’s or any of the other Ashford-Related Entities’ personnel or conduct and ethics policies or breach of fiduciary duty. SEPARATION AGREEMENT – Page 6 Confidentiality . Subject to Section 4(a) above, Employee agrees to keep confidential and not to disclose (or authorize another to disclose) the existence or terms of this Agreement, except that the foregoing obligation does not include disclosures: (i) to his/her immediate family members, attorney, or tax or financial advisors, if any, provided any such disclosures are made in a confidential manner or setting and limited to the purpose of the disclosure; (ii) to a governmental agency if requested in connection with an investigation or otherwise in the exercise of Employee’s rights under Section 4(a) above; (iii) if compelled by law or valid judicial process; or (iv) as necessary in any legal proceeding to enforce this Agreement. 8. Non-Disparagement Obligations of the Parties . (a) Subject to Section 4(a) above, Employee agrees not to make, or authorize another to make, any statement (oral, written, or electronic) to the media, on social media, or to any “third party” which directly or indirectly impugns the integrity, skills, competence, business, operations, management, prospects, or personnel affairs of any of the Released Parties. “ Third party ” for purposes of this subsection does not include statements made: (x) to or between Employee and his/her immediate family members, attorney, or tax or financial advisors, if any, in a confidential manner or setting, if such persons have agreed to keep such information confidential; (y) in the exercise of Employee’s rights under Section 4(a) above; or (z) as necessary in any legal proceeding to enforce this Agreement. (b) Subject to Section 5(b) above, the Company (on behalf of itself and AINC) agrees that it will not authorize the making of any statement (oral, written, or electronic) to the·media, on social media, or to any “third party” which directly or indirectly impugns the integrity, shills, or competence of Employee. “ Third party ” for purposes of this subsection does not include statements made (w) made to or between any of the Ashford Entities or any of their personnel; (x) to or between any of the Ashford Entities’ attorneys, accountants, tax or financial, advisors, insurers, or auditors; (y) in the exercise of it or their rights under Section 5(b) above; (z) otherwise made for legitimate business-related purposes (such as may be necessary for the implementation of this Agreement or in connection with a legal filing or business transaction); or (aa) as necessary in any legal proceeding to enforce this Agreement. 9. Time for Review; Acceptance; Effective Date; Right to Revoke . Employee may accept this Agreement by signing below and returning the signed copy to the attention of Nicole Shanks, Chief Human Resources Officer at 14185 Dallas Parkway, Suite 1150, Dallas, Texas 75254 or to NicoleShanks@RemingtonHotels.com , no later than the close of business on the 45th day after he/she first received the Agreement and the OWBPA Chart. The Agreement will become effective and enforceable eight days after he/she signs and returns it (the “ Effective Date ”). At any time before the Effective Date, Employee may revoke his/her acceptance of the Agreement by sending written notice of revocation to the attention of Nicole Shanks, Chief Human Resources Officer at 14185 Dallas Parkway, Suite 1150, Dallas, Texas 75254 or to NicoleShanks@RemingtonHotels.com . If Employee does timely revoke his/her acceptance, he will not be entitled to and will not receive the Separation Benefit. SEPARATION AGREEMENT – Page 7 10. Acknowledgments . By signing this Agreement, Employee acknowledges and agrees that: (i) he/she has read this Agreement and the OWBPA Chart; (ii) he/she is hereby advised to consult an attorney about the meaning and effect of this Agreement; (iii) he/she has had sufficient time to consider this Agreement and to consult an attorney if he/she wished to do so; (iv) he/she fully understands the meaning and effect of signing this Agreement; (v) he/she is not relying on any written or oral statement or promise from any of the Released Parties that is not set out in this Agreement, but instead is relying on his/her own judgment in consultation with his/her attorney, if any. This Agreement (or the offering or accepting of it) does not in any manner constitute an admission of liability or wrongdoing by Employee or any of the Ashford-Related Entities, and except to the extent necessary to enforce this Agreement, neither this Agreement nor any part of it may be construed as, used, or admitted into evidence in any judicial, administrative, or arbitral proceeding, as an admission of any kind. 11. Entire Agreement; Choice of Law; Jurisdiction and Venue; Jury-Trial Waiver . The Parties agree that: (i) this Agreement contains and constitutes the entire understanding and agreement between Employee and the Released Parties relating to his/her separation from employment, and supersedes all other agreements and understandings between him/herself and any of the Released Parties related to their employment by the Company and separation therefrom; (ii) this Agreement shall be construed and enforced in accordance with, and is governed by the laws of the State of Texas, without reference to any choice of law principles that would require the application of the law of another jurisdiction; (iii) this Agreement has been negotiated by the Parties; (iv) this Agreement is to be construed as a whole, according to its fair meaning, and not strictly for or against Employee or the Company or the other Released Parties; (v) each will submit and consent to the exclusive jurisdiction, including removal jurisdiction, of the state and federal courts located in Dallas County, Texas for any action or proceeding relating to this Agreement, Employee’s employment by the Company, or the ending of his/her employment; (vi) each hereby waives any objection to such venue; and (vii) the Company (on behalf of itself and the other Ashford-Related Entities and Released Parties) and Employee irrevocably waive the right to trial by jury and agree not to ask for a jury in any such proceeding . 12. Miscellaneous . (a) Non-Assignment . Employee acknowledges and agrees that: (i) he/she has no right to assign or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any of his/her rights or obligations under this Agreement; (ii) he/she has no right to pledge, hypothecate, anticipate, or in any way create a lien upon any payments or other benefits provided under this Agreement; and (iii) no amounts payable under this Agreement shall be assignable in anticipation of payment either by voluntary or involuntary acts, or by operation of law, except by will or pursuant to the laws of descent and distribution. (b) Binding Effect; Third-Party Beneficiaries . This Agreement is binding upon the Parties and their successors and assigns, and shall inure to the benefit of the Parties and their successors and assigns. The Released Parties are intended third-party beneficiaries of this Agreement. (c) Severability . If any provision (or portion thereof) of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unenforceable: (i) then such provision (or portion thereof) shall be considered separate, distinct, and severable from the remaining provisions of this Agreement, and shall not affect the validity or enforceability of such other provisions; and (ii) such invalid or unenforceable provision (or portion thereof) may be made to be enforceable by limitation, then such provision (or portion thereof) shall be enforceable to the maximum extent permitted by law. SEPARATION AGREEMENT – Page 8 (d) Counterparts . This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall be considered one and the same agreement. The delivery of this Agreement in the form of a clearly legible facsimile or electronically scanned version by email shall have the same force and effect as delivery of the originally executed document. ACCEPTED AND AGREED: /s/ Justin Coe November 3, 2026 Justin Coe Date Signed ASHFORD HOSPITALITY ADVISORS LLC /s/ Jim Plohg November 2, 2026 By: Jim Plohg Date Signed Title: EVP SEPARATION AGREEMENT – Page 9

title: AMERICAN REBEL HOLDINGS INC
text: EX-10.1 3 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 THE EXCHANGE CONTEMPLATED HEREIN IS INTENDED TO COMPORT WITH THE REQUIREMENTS OF SECTION 3(a)(9) OF THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED. EXCHANGE AGREEMENT This Exchange Agreement (this “ Agreement ”) is entered into as of October 30, 2026 by and between Horberg Enterprises, LP (“ Investor ”), and American Rebel Holdings, Inc., a Nevada corporation (“ Company ”). A. Company previously sold and issued to Investor 100,000 shares of Series D Convertible Preferred Stock, valued at $7.50 per share (the “ Series D Preferred ”) pursuant to that certain Securites Purchase Agreement entered into as of October 1, 2025. B. Company and Investor desire to exchange (such exchange is referred to as the “ Exchange ”) 6,800 shares of Series D Preferred (the “ Preferred Shares ”) with an aggregate Stated Value (as such term is defined in the Certificate of Designation of Preferences and Rights of Series D Preferred Stock) of $51,000.00 for 51 shares of Company’s Series E Preferred Stock (the “ Exchange Shares ”), at an effective price per Exchange Share of $1,000.00, according to the terms and conditions of this Agreement. C. The Exchange will consist of Investor surrendering the Preferred Shares in exchange for the Exchange Shares. D. Other than the surrender of the Preferred Shares, no consideration of any kind whatsoever shall be given by Investor to Company in connection with this Agreement. E. Investor and Company now desire to exchange the Preferred Shares for the Exchange Shares on the terms and conditions set forth herein. NOW, THEREFORE, for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows: 1. Recitals and Definitions . Each of the parties hereto acknowledges and agrees that the recitals set forth above in this Agreement are true and accurate, are contractual in nature, and are hereby incorporated into and made a part of this Agreement. 2. Issuance of Exchange Shares . Pursuant to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Exchange Shares will be issued to Investor on or before October 30, 2026 (such date, the “ Issuance Date ”) and the Exchange will occur with Investor surrendering the Preferred Shares to Company on the Issuance Date. On the Issuance Date, the Preferred Shares will be cancelled and all obligations of Company under the Preferred Shares shall be deemed fulfilled. The Exchange Shares be issued in book entry form with Company’s securities counsel. 3. Closing . The closing of the Exchange shall occur on the Effective Date by means of the exchange by express courier and email of .pdf documents, but shall be deemed to have occurred at the offices of DeMint Law, PLLC in Las Vegas, Nevada. 4. Holding Period, Tacking and Legal Opinion . Company represents, warrants and agrees that for the purposes of Rule 144 (“ Rule 144 ”) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “ Securities Act ”), the holding period of the Exchange Shares will include Investor’s holding period of the Preferred Shares from October 1, 2025. Company agrees not to take a position contrary to this Section 4 in any document, statement, setting, or situation. The Exchange Shares are being issued in substitution of and exchange for and not in satisfaction of the Preferred Shares. The Exchange Shares shall not constitute a novation or satisfaction and accord of the Preferred Shares. Company acknowledges and understands that the representations and agreements of Company in this Section 4 are a material inducement to Investor’s decision to consummate the transactions contemplated herein. 5. Company’s Representations, Warranties and Agreements . text: EX-10.1 5 d11042026ex101.htm SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT Exhibit 10.1 REGULATION S SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT ORIGIN TEA INC. 2,500 Shares of Common Stock This Regulation S Subscription Agreement (this “Agreement”) is submitted to Origin Tea Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “Company”), by the purchaser identified on Schedule A (the “Purchaser”). The Purchaser confirms the subscription commitment and funding described in Schedule A and offers to purchase 2,500 shares of the Company’s common stock (the “Shares”), subject to written acceptance by the Company. 1. Offering; Subscription; Prior Funding The Company authorized a private placement of up to 500,000 shares of its common stock at a stated offering price of US$6.00 per share, with a fixed RMB subscription and settlement price of RMB 40.00 per share for subscriptions funded in Renminbi. The Offering was closed to new subscription commitments after August 31, 2026. Each standard subscription consists of 2,500 Shares for total subscription consideration of RMB 100,000. The Purchaser represents that, on the Funding Date specified in Schedule A and no later than August 31, 2026, the Purchaser, or an approved third-party remitter identified in Schedule D, transmitted RMB 100,000 in connection with the Offering to Hainan Baisha Yuanwu Yayun Tea Co., Ltd. (海南白沙源物雅韵茶叶有限公司) (“Baisha Yuanwu”), the Company’s indirect wholly owned PRC subsidiary designated by the Board solely as the Company’s collection agent for RMB subscription funds. Payment to Baisha Yuanwu for the account of the Company constitutes delivery of the subscription funds to the Company for purposes of this Agreement, subject to Company acceptance or refund. The Purchaser acknowledges that the prior remittance was made in anticipation of the subscription, remained pending and refundable before Company acceptance, and did not by itself constitute Company acceptance, issuance of any Share, or admission of the Purchaser as a stockholder. The Company may reject the subscription before acceptance, in which case the subscription funds shall be returned to the remitting account, without interest, less unavoidable bank charges if any. 2. Acceptance; Closing; Issuance This Agreement is not binding on the Company until it is countersigned by Xiangying Meng or another duly authorized officer on behalf of the Company. The closing of this subscription (the “Closing”) occurs only after the Company has: (a) received this completed Agreement and requested identity and compliance documentation; (b) verified the Purchaser’s subscription funds and funding information; (c) reasonably determined that the offer and sale satisfy Regulation S; and (d) accepted the subscription. At Closing, the Company shall cause 2,500 Shares to be issued to the Purchaser in restricted book-entry form through the Company’s transfer agent or stock ledger. The Shares shall be validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable when issued in accordance with the Board resolutions and this Agreement. No certificate or book-entry statement shall be interpreted to remove any restriction described in this Agreement or applicable law. 3. Purchaser Representations, Warranties and Covenants 3.1. The Purchaser is not a “U.S. person” as defined in Rule 902(k) of Regulation S, and the Purchaser was outside the United States when the investment decision and buy order/subscription instruction were made and when this Agreement was executed. 3.2. The Purchaser is acquiring the Shares for the Purchaser’s own account and not for the account or benefit of any U.S. person. No undisclosed U.S. person has any direct or indirect beneficial interest in the subscription. 3.3. The offer and sale are offshore transactions. The Purchaser has not been solicited through directed selling efforts in the United States and has not entered into any arrangement designed to evade the registration requirements of the Securities Act. 3.4. The Purchaser understands that the Shares have not been registered under the Securities Act or state securities laws and are restricted securities. The Purchaser will not offer, sell, assign, pledge, hedge or otherwise transfer the Shares except in compliance with Regulation S, pursuant to an effective registration statement, or pursuant to another available exemption from registration. 3.5. During the applicable Regulation S distribution compliance period, the Purchaser will comply with the purchaser certification, notice, resale and hedging restrictions applicable to Category 3 equity securities of a U.S. reporting issuer. The Purchaser understands that expiration of that period does not itself make the Shares freely tradable. 3.6 . The Purchaser understands that the Company has previously been identified as a shell company and that Rule 144(i), current-public-information requirements, holding periods and other legal conditions may restrict or delay resale or legend removal. The Company makes no representation that Rule 144 will be available on any particular date. 3.7 . The Purchaser has sufficient knowledge and experience to evaluate the merits and risks of the investment, has reviewed information made available by the Company, has had the opportunity to ask questions, can bear the complete loss of the subscription amount, and is not relying on any promise of liquidity, market value, dividend, listing, quotation or future financing, except for the express contractual registration rights set forth in Section 5 of this Agreement. 3.8 . The Purchaser has full legal capacity and authority to enter into this Agreement. If the Purchaser is an entity, it is duly organized, its signatory is duly authorized, and the Purchaser shall complete Schedule B and provide the entity and beneficial ownership information and supporting documentation reasonably requested by the Company. 3.9 . The subscription funds and the Purchaser’s wealth are derived from lawful activity. The Purchaser, each beneficial owner and the remitting account holder are not persons with whom the Company is prohibited from dealing under applicable sanctions, anti-money-laundering or other laws. The Purchaser will provide supporting documentation reasonably requested by the Company. 3.10 . All information supplied by the Purchaser in Schedule A and related diligence materials is accurate, complete and not misleading in any material respect, and the Purchaser will promptly notify the Company of any material change before Closing. 3.11 . The Purchaser is responsible for compliance with applicable securities, foreign-exchange, tax and other laws of the Purchaser’s jurisdiction. The Company has not provided foreign-law or tax advice to the Purchaser. 3.12 . The Purchaser has not retained or authorized any broker, dealer, finder or placement agent who may claim compensation from the Company in connection with this subscription, except as separately disclosed in writing to and approved by the Company. 4. Company Representations and Covenants 4.1. The Company is a Nevada corporation and the Board has authorized the Offering and the issuance of the Shares subject to the terms of this Agreement. 4.2. Baisha Yuanwu has been designated by the Board as the Company’s collection agent for RMB subscription funds for this Offering. No ownership interest in Baisha Yuanwu is being offered or issued under this Agreement. 4.3. The Company and persons acting on its behalf shall not make directed selling efforts in the United States in connection with the Offering and shall implement the offering restrictions required by Regulation S. 4.4. The Company shall maintain appropriate restrictive legends and stop-transfer instructions and may refuse to register any transfer that does not comply with applicable securities laws and the terms of this Agreement. 5. Registration Rights 5.1 Filing of Resale Registration Statement. The Company shall promptly commence preparation following the Closing and, as soon as reasonably practicable thereafter, prepare and file with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) a registration statement on Form S-1, or such other appropriate registration form as may then be available to the Company (the “Resale Registration Statement”), covering the resale by the Purchaser and the other accepted purchasers in the Offering of all Shares issued in the Offering that constitute Registrable Securities. The Company shall not unreasonably delay the filing and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to respond to SEC comments and to cause the Resale Registration Statement to be declared effective as soon as reasonably practicable after filing. The parties acknowledge that the timing of filing and effectiveness may depend on completion of required financial statements and audits, SEC review, legal and accounting requirements, and other matters outside the Company’s reasonable control. 5.2 Registrable Securities. “Registrable Securities” means the Shares issued to the Purchaser pursuant to this Agreement, and any shares issued or issuable with respect to such Shares by reason of a stock split, stock dividend, recapitalization or similar transaction, for so long as such securities are held by the Purchaser or a permitted transferee and have not (a) been sold pursuant to an effective registration statement, (b) been sold pursuant to Rule 144 or another exemption in a transaction after which the securities are no longer restricted, or (c) otherwise become freely transferable without registration under the Securities Act as determined by the Company in good faith upon advice of securities counsel. 5.3 Maintenance and Amendments. Following effectiveness, the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to keep the Resale Registration Statement effective and the related prospectus current and usable for resales of the Registrable Securities until no Registrable Securities remain. The Company shall file such amendments, post-effective amendments and prospectus supplements as are reasonably necessary for that purpose and shall take such other actions as are reasonably necessary to permit lawful resale under the Resale Registration Statement. 5.4 Purchaser Cooperation. As a condition to being named as a selling stockholder and using the Resale Registration Statement, the Purchaser shall timely provide all information, questionnaires, certifications and updates reasonably requested by the Company or its counsel, including information concerning beneficial ownership, broker-dealer or affiliate status, plan of distribution and the Shares proposed to be registered. The Company may omit the Purchaser from the initial filing or temporarily suspend the Purchaser’s use of the prospectus if required information has not been timely provided, without constituting a breach of this Section, provided the Company uses commercially reasonable efforts to include the Purchaser promptly after the required information is received. 5.5 Registration Expenses. The Company shall bear the SEC registration and filing fees and the reasonable fees and expenses of the Company’s legal counsel, independent accountants and other professionals incurred in preparing, filing and maintaining the Resale Registration Statement. The Purchaser shall bear all brokerage commissions, underwriting or selling discounts, transfer taxes, and the fees and expenses of any separate legal or other adviser engaged by the Purchaser in connection with any resale. 5.6 Suspension of Use. The Company may require the Purchaser to suspend use of the prospectus for the shortest period reasonably practicable when use of the prospectus would violate applicable law, when an SEC stop order or similar proceeding is pending, when the prospectus requires a material amendment or supplement, or when the Board determines in good faith that disclosure of material nonpublic information at that time would be materially detrimental to the Company. The Company shall notify affected purchasers when use may resume, subject to applicable law and confidentiality obligations. 5.7 Registration Indemnification. To the extent permitted by law, the Company shall indemnify the Purchaser against liabilities under the Securities Act arising from any material misstatement or omission in the Resale Registration Statement or related prospectus, except to the extent arising from information furnished in writing by or on behalf of the Purchaser specifically for inclusion therein or from the Purchaser’s unlawful use of a prospectus after notice of suspension. The Purchaser shall indemnify the Company and its directors, officers and controlling persons against such liabilities to the extent arising from written information supplied by the Purchaser specifically for inclusion in the registration statement or prospectus; provided that the Purchaser’s aggregate liability under this sentence shall not exceed the net proceeds actually received by the Purchaser from the sale of Registrable Securities giving rise to the liability, except in the case of fraud or willful misconduct. 5.8 No Guarantee of Effectiveness or Market. The registration rights in this Section are contractual obligations to use the efforts expressly stated above and do not constitute a guarantee that the SEC will declare the Resale Registration Statement effective by any particular date, that any market for the Shares will exist, or that any resale can be completed at any particular price or time. Until a resale is made pursuant to an effective registration statement or an available exemption, the Shares remain subject to the transfer restrictions in this Agreement and applicable law. 6. Transfer Restrictions; Legend Because the Company is a U.S. reporting issuer, the Company intends to treat the Shares as Category 3 equity securities under Regulation S and to apply the applicable six-month distribution compliance period beginning at completion of the Offering, subject to confirmation under applicable law. For this coordinated Offering, the Company currently expects the distribution compliance period to run through May 4, 2027. Any longer restriction applicable under the Securities Act, Rule 144, Rule 144(i), state law, the Company’s governing documents or transfer-agent procedures remains in effect notwithstanding the expiration of that Regulation S period. THEY MAY NOT BE OFFERED, SOLD, ASSIGNED, PLEDGED, HEDGED OR OTHERWISE TRANSFERRED EXCEPT IN ACCORDANCE WITH REGULATION S UNDER THE ACT, PURSUANT TO AN EFFECTIVE REGISTRATION STATEMENT UNDER THE ACT, OR PURSUANT TO AN AVAILABLE EXEMPTION FROM REGISTRATION.
